If the journal reports ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'bmp280', install the driver into the same Python environment used to run PHOS. On the Raspberry Pi, for the documented installation:

cd ~/phos
.venv/bin/python -m pip install 'bmp280>=1.0.0,<2' 'smbus2>=0.4,<1'
.venv/bin/python -c "import bmp280, smbus2; print('Driver OK')"

The sensor service retries automatically after installation. To restart the managed service explicitly:

systemctl --user restart phos.service
journalctl --user -u phos.service -n 100 --no-pager

For a manual launch, stop and rerun PHOS with the same virtual environment. Selecting BMP280 in Web Admin does not install its optional Python dependency. If imports succeed but the runtime still reports a missing module, check that the service uses this virtual environment and checkout.

The sensor type in the warning is the active runtime selection. For BMP280, the deployed sensors.environmental block must have "type": "bmp280" and "enabled": true. Check the configuration path shown in Web Admin → System / Status; a development-machine file may differ from the Pi's file. Saved sensor configuration changes require Restart PHOS even though driver failures retry automatically.

docs.title: Optional GY-521 / MPU-6050 IMU
docs.text:
PHOS reads the GY-521's MPU-6050 accelerometer and gyroscope on I2C bus 1. Stop PHOS before wiring or probing the bus. Connect VCC to 3.3 V, GND to GND, SDA to GPIO2/pin 3, and SCL to GPIO3/pin 5. Ensure the specific breakout uses 3.3 V I2C logic. Leave INT/XDA/XCL unconnected. AD0 low is 0x68; AD0 high is 0x69.

systemctl --user stop phos.service
i2cdetect -y 1 0x68 0x69
cd ~/phos
.venv/bin/python -m pip install 'smbus2>=0.4,<1'
.venv/bin/python -m pip check

Expect 68 or 69; -- means no response and UU means another driver owns the device. The optional package extra is .[imu]. Merge the complete sensors.imu block from config/phos.yaml into an existing configuration, then enable it in Web Admin → Sensors → GY-521 / MPU-6050 motion (or set "enabled": true directly). All four fields require Restart PHOS:

cd ~/phos
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -c "from robot.config import ConfigRepository; ConfigRepository().load(); print('Configuration valid')"
systemctl --user restart phos.service
journalctl --user -u phos.service -n 100 --no-pager

The status panel shows acceleration X/Y/Z in m/s² and angular velocity X/Y/Z in °/s, with timestamp, age and health. PHOS configures ±2 g / ±250 °/s and converts the raw readings using factory scale factors. It does not calibrate mounting offsets at startup: keep the robot still only when comparing baseline values, and expect one acceleration axis to include gravity. The interpreter estimates tilt from gravity; no full orientation fusion is implemented. If other Pi I2C devices share bus 1, retain their documented 10 kHz i2c_arm_baudrate setting.

The motion interpreter prioritizes IMPACT, SHAKE, confirmed TILT, MOVING, then STILL. Tilt no longer requires the movement metric to be below threshold. It low-pass filters acceleration with a fixed 0.2-second time constant using sample elapsed time, then normalizes the gravity vector. The existing tilt_threshold_m_s2 remains the enter setting, now measured as normalized lateral/forward gravity component times standard gravity, independent of total acceleration magnitude. Default 4.0 corresponds to about 24°; tilt_exit_threshold_m_s2 defaults to 3.0 (about 18°). A confirmed direction holds until below exit; otherwise the largest component wins (lateral wins exact ties). confirmation_seconds defaults to 0.3 for entry, direction changes and exit. Brief vibration cannot confirm a tilt. At the default 0.05-second IMU poll interval (20 Hz), a normal 35° tilt settles in roughly half a second. Existing five-second polling deployments must change that setting and restart to obtain this responsiveness. Slower polling necessarily limits confirmation speed.

Mounting is explicit: lateral_axis and forward_axis each select a distinct signed sensor axis (x, -x, y, -y, z, -z). Defaults retain the old X/Y convention: positive mapped lateral acceleration means TILT_RIGHT, negative means TILT_LEFT; positive mapped forward means TILT_FORWARD, negative means TILT_BACK. At level, both mapped components should be near zero, with gravity on the unused axis. Verify by physically tilting right and forward; reverse signs or swap axes as needed. No startup calibration assumes that the robot is level. Diagnostic roll/pitch are asin(mapped normalized lateral/forward) in degrees: approximate signed inclinations, not full Euler attitude or yaw. Upside-down orientation is not distinguished. Sustained linear acceleration cannot be fully distinguished from gravity by this accelerometer-only method; freefall-like filtered magnitudes below 0.25 g do not provide tilt evidence.

Movement still compares filtered acceleration magnitude with gravity (default 1.5 m/s²); shake requires opposite high gyro samples (180 °/s); impact uses raw total acceleration (25 m/s²). Both override tilt. The event cooldown (2 seconds) does not delay stable state publication. All motion settings apply through Web Admin → Sensors → GY-521 / MPU-6050 motion → Save → Reload configuration, without reopening I2C. Reload clears pending tilt evidence and filter history. Enable DEBUG logging temporarily to see IMU motion diagnostics at most once per second: filtered acceleration, pitch/roll, movement metric, normalized enter/exit thresholds, tilt candidate, winning classification/reason, confirmed state and confirmation duration. MOVING explains whether gravity is too small or tilt is below threshold; a pending tilt leaves the previous state visible until confirmation completes.

To test motion interpretation on the Pi: rest level, tilt each direction about 35° and hold one second, gently vibrate while holding tilt, then return level. Confirm STILL → the correct TILT → STILL in status and diagnostics; level vertical movement should produce MOVING. Verify mounting signs before assessing eye reactions. Save/reload thresholds and confirm the provider is not reopened.

With visual reactions enabled, sustained tilt visibly moves pupils in the tilt direction and remains active while tilt is observed. Defaults use 86% of the safe gaze range. Horizontal tilt uses imu_tilt_eye_asymmetry_strength 0.18: TILT*LEFT opens the left eye and closes the right by the same amount; TILT_RIGHT mirrors it. Left/right use shared openness 1.12 before that split; forward and back keep equal eyes at 1.23 and 0.82 respectively. MOVING recenters pupils, opens to 1.16 and uses 0.63 reaction strength. SHAKE is a 1.18-open, 0.88-strength surprised alert for 1.35 seconds; IMPACT is the stronger 1.25-open, 1.0-strength alert for 1.0 second. Both hold for 55% of the duration and then decay smoothly. Configure the eight behavior.imu*\* values in Web Admin → Display & Appearance → Eye behavior, save and use Reload configuration. Impact strength must remain greater than shake strength. The base iris theme returns after an alert because the alert is temporary semantic tint, not an appearance change.

To test motion effects on the display, enable the IMU and DEBUG logging, then confirm that MOVING recenters the pupils, each held tilt produces the documented gaze direction and mirrored eye-size change, SHAKE produces a clear amber surprised response and IMPACT is visibly wider/brighter/stronger. Let each alert expire and verify the configured iris theme returns. Confirm sleeping, speaking and error remain visually authoritative over IMU intent.

On the Pi, verify the detected address and WHO_AM_I, stable six-axis values, wrong-address recovery, a restart, and coexistence with every connected I2C sensor. Record the board revision and wiring.

docs.title: Optional WS2812B RGB LED ring
docs.text:
Connect the WS2812B addressable RGB LED ring to the ESP32 controller. The Pi sends semantic LED commands over phos-hw v1 USB/serial JSONL. ESP32 firmware drives the data line, pixel ordering, LED count, and timing.

Build and flash the official phos-esp32 firmware using its instructions for your board and attached sensors/LED ring. Then configure the PHOS serial connection below.

docs.title: Enable the serial controller
docs.text:
Edit these fields in the complete canonical config/phos.yaml; retain the other configuration sections:

hardware_controller:
  enabled: true
  transport: serial
  serial:
    device: /dev/ttyACM0
    baud_rate: 115200
    dtr: false
    rts: false
  reconnect:
    delay_seconds: 2
  heartbeat:
    interval_seconds: 5
    timeout_seconds: 15

Use the actual serial device and firmware baud rate. Ensure the PHOS user has serial-device access and that the cable carries USB data. The installer includes pySerial through the hardware-controller extra.

Keep led_ring.enabled: false. That separate legacy configuration block does not enable or configure the ESP32 semantic LED path. Do not install a local LED helper or use its pin/count settings for this build.

Start PHOS using the documented foreground or managed-service launch. In Web Admin's Hardware Controller view, confirm a connected session and a fresh capabilities report advertising LED support. The adapter recognizes led_count, led.count, or "led" in a capabilities list; for example, the controller may report:

{"protocol":"phos-hw","version":1,"type":"capabilities","payload":{"led":{"count":12}}}

The example count describes the ring fitted to the controller; configure its actual pin, count, and channel ordering in firmware. PHOS suppresses LED commands until both connection and advertised capability are available.

docs.title: Check semantic output
docs.text:
Use a permitted MCP phos_signal_user request or the semantic Remote API signal action. PHOS arbitrates the request and sends a bounded set_led_animation command; the ESP32 executes it. Check that temporary signals expire and the persistent intent returns, then reconnect the controller and confirm intent reapplication after capability discovery.

Power the ring from an appropriately sized supply, share ground between ESP32 and LED supply, and use data-level shifting where the ring requires it. Refer to the hardware wiring notes and the controller protocol for message and direction semantics.

docs.title: Controller-backed ENS160 and AHT21
docs.text:
ENS160 and AHT21 are connected to the ESP32 shared I2C bus, not Raspberry Pi I2C. ENS160 uses 0x53 (or 0x52) and AHT21 uses 0x38. The controller publishes measurements and status through phos-hw v1 JSON Lines, so PHOS needs no Pi-side driver, I2C setup, optional package, or migration for either device.

Use phos-esp32 for ENS160 + AHT21 telemetry; follow its build/flashing instructions and select the matching I2C wiring. Verify ESP32 wiring and the serial controller connection. The Sensors page reports sensors.ens160 with estimated eCO2 (ppm), TVOC (ppb), AQI-UBA (1–5), validity and compensation status, and sensors.aht21 with controller temperature and relative humidity. eCO2 is an estimate, not direct NDIR CO2. During ENS160 startup or warm-up, and after disconnects, PHOS withholds unusable gas values while independently fresh AHT21 and BMP280/BME280 values remain available. A reconnect requires fresh telemetry for its new controller session.

docs.title: ENS160/AHT21 verification
docs.text: Confirm the ESP32 controller is connected and advertises sensor capability, then inspect Sensors status for fresh sensors.ens160 and sensors.aht21 records. ENS160 gas values are usable only when validity and freshness permit them; AHT21 freshness is independent. Diagnose missing readings through controller serial telemetry, ESP32 wiring and power, rather than Raspberry Pi I2C tools.

docs.title: MCP — Eyes, voice and senses for AI agents
docs.text:
Give your agent physical context and a way to communicate through PHOS. Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides the resources and tools connecting the external application to the local runtime. PHOS provides perception and controlled execution; the external agent supplies reasoning and decisions.

flowchart LR
  P[Physical observations] --> S[PHOS semantic services]
  S -->|Resources and update cues| A[External MCP client / agent]
  A -->|Tools| G[Identity and permission checks]
  G --> S --> O[Eyes, speech and LED signals]

PHOS can run on its own, but MCP lets a compatible, authenticated agent ask about the robot's current context and request supported actions. PHOS continues to own hardware, robot state, safety boundaries, and permission checks.

docs.title: Connect a local stdio client
docs.text:
Use the recommended phos-mcp-bridge transport adapter (Node.js 20+) when connecting a compatible client through local stdio. It forwards requests to http://<PHOS_IP>:8001/mcp; use the Pi's actual address and configured listener or a tunnel to the default loopback endpoint. Clients with native Streamable HTTP support may connect directly.

flowchart LR
  client[Local MCP client] <-->|stdio| bridge[phos-mcp-bridge]
  bridge <-->|Streamable HTTP / bearer| phos[PHOS application services]
  phos <-->|phos-hw v1 serial JSONL| controller[Optional compatible controller]

Supply the PHOS-issued bearer through the bridge's PHOS_MCP_TOKEN environment variable, never CLI flags or URLs. PHOS authenticates the request and enforces permissions; the bridge only transports it. The bridge never automatically retries tools/call, because a physical action may already have happened before a response was lost. Check state before manually repeating a request. Follow the client quickstart for connection setup. For optional controllers, see the hardware protocol.

docs.title: Ask PHOS or request an action
docs.text:
These synchronous interactions return a result to the caller. Availability depends on configured hardware and services; unavailable or degraded capabilities are reported rather than assumed to work.

Capability What an agent can do Interface Access Robot status Read robot state, available capabilities, and degraded conditions. phos_get_status, phos://status Observer or standard Physical context Read available environment, air-quality, motion, presence, attention, and observed-expression semantics. phos_get_physical_context, phos://physical-context Observer or standard Environment Read temperature, humidity where available, pressure, and interpreted conditions with availability/freshness context; air-quality measurements are in physical context. phos://environment Observer or standard Presence and attention Read whether people are present and the semantic attention state—never identity. phos_get_presence, phos_get_attention Observer or standard Observed expression Read a bounded visible-expression classification; it is not an emotion or identity claim. phos_get_observed_expression Observer or standard Physical evidence Assess retained measurement coverage, freshness, and recovery evidence before interpreting history. phos_get_physical_assessment, phos://physical-context/assessment History permission required Retained context Query bounded RAM-only measurements or confirmed transitions. phos_query_measurements, phos_list_physical_transitions History permission required Object awareness Request one on-demand, local NanoDet observation when configured. phos_get_visible_objects Perception permission required Camera observation Retrieve a privacy-bounded JPEG from the latest cached frame, or wait for the next pipeline frame, when camera access is permitted. phos_get_camera_snapshot, phos_capture_camera_snapshot, phos://vision/snapshot Standard only Expression Request a supported PHOS expression. phos_set_expression Standard only Thinking visual state Request a bounded agent-owned thinking visual state, or release it. phos_set_state Standard only Voice Ask PHOS to speak bounded text through configured TTS. phos_speak Standard only Robot state Request normal sleep or wake transitions. phos_sleep, phos_wake Standard only Semantic signal Request a supported, transient controller-backed LED signal. phos_signal_user Standard only

An observer profile is deliberately read-only. A standard profile can use the currently exposed semantic actions and, when camera is available, the protected snapshot Resource. PHOS checks permissions on every authenticated request; a client never receives direct GPIO, serial-controller, or renderer access. See the MCP reference for the exact endpoint, authentication, and credential lifecycle.

docs.title: Tool and Resource Catalog
docs.text:
All tools return structured semantic results; tools without arguments take {}.

Tool Arguments Access Purpose / limit phos_get_status, phos_get_physical_context, phos_get_presence, phos_get_attention, phos_get_observed_expression None Observer, standard Read compact semantic state. Attention never includes a target identity. phos_get_physical_assessment None read_physical_history Assess bounded evidence; it does not classify trends or prove sensor accuracy. phos_query_measurements required metric; optional time range and limit read_physical_history Read retained samples and summaries; history is RAM-only. phos_list_physical_transitions optional event type and limit read_physical_history Read bounded confirmed semantic transitions. phos_get_visible_objects None read_perception One on-demand NanoDet observation; labels/confidence only. phos_get_camera_snapshot None Standard Returns the existing cached JPEG; PHOS does not interpret it. phos_capture_camera_snapshot None Standard Waits for the next Vision frame; this is not a separate camera exposure. phos_set_expression required expression Standard Requests a supported expression. phos_set_state required state; duration_ms required for thinking Standard thinking lasts 250–60000 ms; idle releases the caller's lease. phos_speak required text (1–500 characters) Standard Requests bounded TTS; physical side effect. phos_sleep, phos_wake None Standard Request normal robot-state transitions; physical side effect. phos_signal_user required signal Standard Requests a supported transient signal; physical side effect. Resource Access and use Update cue phos://status Observer/standard compact robot status. Yes phos://physical-context Observer/standard anonymous environment, motion, presence, attention, and observed expression. Yes phos://physical-context/assessment History permission required; bounded evidence and source availability. Yes phos://environment Observer/standard environmental context. Yes phos://vision/snapshot Standard-only cached JPEG for external multimodal interpretation. No — intentionally on-demand.

Use resources/read with the URI. Camera images are separate from notification delivery and may contain people visible to the camera.

docs.title: React to changes
docs.text:
MCP resource subscriptions provide asynchronous change cues, not long-running tool jobs and not unsolicited chat messages. A subscribing client decides what to do after it is notified. PHOS uses the subscriptions/listen mechanism from MCP revision 2026-07-28, through the supported Python SDK 2.x line. See the official resource specification and subscription lifecycle.

Discovery (resources/list) identifies resources. A read (resources/read) returns current contents. To receive change cues, keep a subscriptions/listen request open with the desired URIs in notifications.resourceSubscriptions. The SDK acknowledges the stream and delivers notifications/resources/updated with a URI and subscription correlation metadata. That notification carries no measurements; read the resource again to obtain current context.

Numeric measurement updates alone do not trigger these cues. Confirmed semantic conditions and relevant availability/freshness changes do. This lets a compatible client wait for meaningful changes without continuously polling, while periodic numerical analysis still needs explicit reads or bounded history queries.

flowchart LR
  subscribe[Subscribe] --> change[PHOS state changes]
  change --> cue[Resource update notification]
  cue --> refresh[Agent refreshes Resource]

The verified subscribable update targets are:

  • phos://status for robot-state, capability, and system-health changes.
  • phos://physical-context for robot-state plus relevant environment, air-quality, motion, presence, attention, and observed-expression changes.
  • phos://environment for relevant environmental condition or availability changes.
  • phos://physical-context/assessment for relevant environmental or air-quality condition and availability changes.

PHOS coalesces repeated update cues. The client rereads the updated Resource to obtain current data. phos://vision/snapshot is readable by authorized clients, but PHOS does not publish subscription updates for it. The separately owned Streamable-HTTP bridge forwards the supported MCP subscription path and can reconnect upstream; client behavior after a disconnection remains the client's responsibility.

Presence and attention are delivered through the same anonymous phos://physical-context cue. A client must re-read it to see the current presence state/count/confidence and semantic attention state; PHOS does not send identities, tracking IDs, or camera images in a notification. These cues are best-effort and have no history: after reconnecting, subscribe again and read the current Resource. They do not automatically make any external AI agent reason or act.

MCP Events is a distinct, future optional protocol capability. PHOS does not advertise or implement it today because its current Python MCP SDK lacks native typed support. This does not affect standard MCP clients or Resource subscriptions.

sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Physical sensors / Vision
  participant P as PHOS runtime and MCP
  participant C as External MCP client / host
  participant A as External agent logic
  participant O as Physical outputs
  C->>P: resources/list and tools/list
  C->>P: subscriptions/listen (physical-context URI)
  P-->>C: notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged
  C->>P: resources/read (initial context)
  P-->>C: Current context
  H->>P: Confirmed presence changes
  P->>P: Update semantic context
  P-->>C: notifications/resources/updated (URI)
  C->>P: resources/read (phos://physical-context)
  P-->>C: Current anonymous presence and context
  C->>A: Provide updated context under host policy
  A->>A: Decide whether to respond
  A->>C: Request supported expression
  C->>P: tools/call (phos_set_expression)
  P->>P: Check identity, permission and runtime
  P->>O: Apply expression through local behavior
  P-->>C: Tool result

The cue does not identify the internal transition that caused it or include an event payload. It is best-effort: adjacent identical semantic transitions can be deduplicated, resource cues can be coalesced, slow clients can lose their bounded stream, and there is no exactly-once delivery, history, or replay.

docs.title: Internal semantic transition mapping
docs.text:
These are not independent MCP subscriptions; clients subscribe by URI and re-read the current state.

Internal transition Notified Resource(s) robot_state_changed status, physical-context environment_condition_changed environment, physical-context, assessment air_quality_condition_changed physical-context, assessment motion_state_changed, presence_changed, attention_changed, observed_expression_changed physical-context capability_changed, system_health_changed status environment_availability_changed environment, physical-context, assessment air_quality_availability_changed physical-context, assessment motion_availability_changed physical-context

PERSON_ENTERED, PERSON_LEFT, attention-target lifecycle events, touch, voice, and raw Vision events are not independently subscribable through MCP.

Read initial context after opening the subscription, and read current context again after reconnecting. PHOS does not replay changes missed during a disconnection. Closing the HTTP stream cancels its listen request; stopping or rebinding the listener ends active streams. Slow clients can lose a bounded stream. External client code owns reconnection, resubscription, and reasoning.

docs.title: Client capabilities and transports
docs.text:
Compatibility depends on the client's implemented protocol and features, not its model or product name. The server uses the official Python SDK 2.x; the transport regression test checks revision 2026-07-28. The table describes requirements, not a certification of individual products.

Client capability Interaction available Compatible Streamable HTTP Direct connection to the running PHOS /mcp endpoint. Compatible local stdio through phos-mcp-bridge Transport adaptation to the same HTTP endpoint; PHOS does not directly serve stdio. Tools only On-demand semantic reads through tools and authorized output calls; no resource UI or subscriptions are assumed. Resources and tools, request/response only Discovery, current-resource reads, and tool calls; external logic initiates refreshes. 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen support Long-lived change cues for the selected PHOS resources, followed by reads and optional tool calls. Legacy resources/subscribe only Does not establish compatibility with PHOS's implemented resource-update path.

The bridge transports requests; it does not add resource support or background reasoning to a host that lacks them. PHOS does not expose a separate legacy SSE endpoint. Inspect a client's actual transport, protocol, credential handling, and notification support before selecting a connection path.

docs.title: Multiple agents and controlled access
docs.text:
Different registered agents can read context and request permitted outputs from one PHOS runtime. Create identities in Settings → Agents, select a profile, and issue independent bearer credentials. Credential creation and rotation show the new value once; existing values cannot be read back. Revocation and registry changes affect subsequent requests without restarting the runtime.

flowchart TD
  observer[Observer agent] -->|Own bearer| auth[PHOS authentication]
  standard[Standard agent] -->|Own bearer| auth
  auth --> permissions[Identity-bound permission checks]
  permissions -->|Permitted reads| context[Shared physical context]
  permissions -->|Permitted actions| services[Application services]
  services --> arbitration[Runtime and output arbitration]
  arbitration --> outputs[Shared physical outputs]

observer can read status, physical context, and perception. standard adds history, camera snapshots, and the exposed semantic actions. Permission is checked before availability and execution; a granted request can still fail because hardware is unavailable or local state prevents it. Discovery of a resource or tool does not grant permission to use it.

Each client has its own connection and subscription streams; identities bind requests to their configured profiles. Resource notifications are URI-only: PHOS authenticates listen requests but does not apply per-resource read permissions to their filters. A client may observe a protected resource's change cue without permission to read its contents. Every read is checked separately; no camera update cues are emitted. Existing streams are not selectively terminated when credentials or permissions change.

Physical outputs are shared. Thinking visuals use identity-owned expiring leases: an agent can release only its own lease, and local error, sleeping, speaking, and listening states retain priority. Other actions use the existing runtime rules; there is no exclusive per-agent display, general action queue, or orchestration guarantee. Coordinate competing agent workflows externally.

PHOS implements its own local bearer registry and permission profiles; it does not implement an OAuth authorization server or external identity provider. MCP supplies the protocol, not an automatic security guarantee. Without any configured credential references, bearer mode retains a credential-free default-agent compatibility path. none and mixed modes also allow an anonymous principal according to configuration. Configure credentials and the appropriate network boundary before relying on distinct authenticated agents. See authentication and security for the complete mode matrix and credential lifecycle.

docs.title: Environmental awareness
docs.text: PHOS provides fresh, availability-aware environmental observations. The agent uses those observations in its own reasoning or response. This is synchronous; it requires the relevant configured sensors and read permission.

docs.title: A physical voice for an agent
docs.text: PHOS provides speech and a supported expression request. The agent decides what to say and when to use it. This is synchronous and requires a standard agent, a working configured TTS path, and the requested supported expression.

docs.title: Presence-aware assistance
docs.text: PHOS provides presence and attention semantics without identifying people. The agent decides whether a response is appropriate. This is synchronous and requires the optional vision pipeline plus read permission.

docs.title: Reactive state monitoring
docs.text: PHOS provides Resource update cues when state changes, such as sleep or wake. The agent subscribes, refreshes the notified Resource, and decides its next step. This is asynchronous and depends on MCP client subscription support.

docs.title: Camera-assisted observation
docs.text: PHOS provides an authorized current snapshot. The agent performs any further visual interpretation. This is synchronous, requires camera availability, and is restricted to the standard profile.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
1. Configure and start PHOS's trusted-local Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint.
  2. Create an agent and credential in Settings → Agents when credential mode is enabled.
  3. Connect a compatible client to the endpoint and provide the bearer through its safe credential mechanism.
  4. Start with status or physical context, then request only capabilities your configured agent is allowed to use.

For connection details, profiles, bearer handling, full tool/resource contracts, remote HTTPS-tunnel guidance, and security considerations for anonymous access, continue to the technical MCP reference.

docs.title: Testing PHOS MCP with MCP Inspector
docs.text:
Use Inspector for discovery, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, and resources/read; select Streamable HTTP and use the configured endpoint (the default is http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp). Supply a bearer only through its secure credential/header mechanism when bearer mode is configured. From a Mac, tunnel first: ssh -L 8001:127.0.0.1:8001 pi@PHOS_HOST.

Read status, physical context, and environment; a standard agent may also read the snapshot JPEG. Test sleep/wake only with deliberate authorization. Inspector versions vary in support for modern long-lived subscriptions/listen; if yours does not expose it, use Inspector for tools/resources and the repository's Python MCP integration test as the transport reference. A compatible SDK client supplies protocol metadata and keeps a request with the following notification filter open:

{"resourceSubscriptions":["phos://physical-context"]}

On a stable presence or attention transition it receives notifications/resources/updated with uri: "phos://physical-context" and SDK subscription correlation metadata, then reads that URI again. After a disconnect, reconnect, resubscribe, and read current state; do not expect historical notifications.

docs.title: MCP reference — physical context and controlled expression
docs.text:
New to MCP with PHOS? Start with MCP — Eyes, voice and senses for AI agents for the capabilities guide.

PHOS starts its trusted-local MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint as part of normal runtime startup. Install the mcp optional dependency, configure mcp in the canonical PHOS configuration, then start PHOS normally:

systemctl --user restart phos.service

PHOS requires Python 3.11 or later for MCP and pins the supported SDK family as mcp>=2.0,<3. The PHOS listener continues to own Uvicorn binding and shutdown; the SDK supplies only the Streamable HTTP ASGI app. This keeps listener lifecycle, Web Admin enable/disable, and port rebinding in McpServerManager. Under SDK 2.x the ASGI app owns the protocol's per-client session handling and its lifespan cleanup; PHOS does not retain SDK session objects. Uvicorn closes that app as part of the existing listener shutdown path.

docs.title: Protocol and SDK references
docs.text:
The supported dependency range allows SDK 2.x rather than locking an exact version. This subscription contract uses MCP revision 2026-07-28, as implemented by SDK 2.3.0 and checked by PHOS's transport regression. PHOS uses MCPServer, InMemorySubscriptionBus, and ResourceUpdated from the official SDK.

Use the 2026-07-28 specification, its resources and subscriptions contracts, and the official Python SDK v2 subscription guide. PHOS publishes its change cues through subscriptions/listen; do not substitute the older resources/subscribe mechanism. For client feature requirements and an end-to-end interaction diagram, see the MCP integration guide.

The committed default endpoint is http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp. MCP is enabled by default, binds only to loopback, and uses one listener in the same process, runtime loop, PhosApplicationService, and AgentApplicationService as PHOS. Each HTTP client has its own MCP session but never creates a runtime or service graph. Stopping PHOS gracefully stops the listener and its sessions. If an enabled endpoint cannot bind, PHOS performs normal shutdown and exits with an error so the service manager applies its configured failure policy.

When Web Administration is enabled, Settings → Network → MCP can enable or disable only this listener and change its port without restarting PHOS. The page and /api/v1/settings/mcp report the actual listener state and endpoint. A failed rebind restores the prior listener and does not persist the requested port; existing client sessions disconnect when a listener is intentionally stopped or rebound. The loopback host and /mcp path remain deliberately non-editable.

mcp:
  enabled: true
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8001
  path: /mcp

Older configuration files without this section retain these defaults. A non-loopback host is allowed only by explicit configuration and emits a warning. Bearer authentication is available when configured, but deployment/TLS policy remains the operator's responsibility; do not expose this endpoint publicly.

docs.title: Agent identity and local compatibility
docs.text:
Every inbound MCP request passes through one authentication middleware boundary before any tool or Resource reaches AgentApplicationService. The middleware resolves an immutable AgentIdentity (id, optional display name, and an existing permission-profile reference); the application facade then applies the existing profile permissions before capability and runtime checks. Identity, permission, capability, and current activity remain separate concerns.

When bearer mode has no configured credential references, the compatibility path resolves the configured default agent without verifying credentials. The committed configuration selects local-agent with the standard profile. This path must not be treated as credential-backed authentication; configure agent credential references and issue credentials to establish independent callers.

The canonical agents configuration persists identities and the default agent. Older configurations without agents retain local-agent/standard. Invalid records, duplicate IDs, unknown profiles, or an unknown default fail loading; no fallback grants broader access. Web Admin updates replace the complete validated registry, so agent create/edit/delete changes apply to subsequent MCP requests without restart.

docs.title: Bearer authentication
docs.text: An agent entry may contain only a non-secret bearer secret_ref. The actual token is read by trusted runtime code from SecretsService, never from runtime configuration or AgentIdentity. If any credential references are configured, identity is request-scoped: every MCP request must provide Authorization: Bearer TOKEN; missing or invalid credentials fail before application execution and never fall back to default_agent. Without credential references, Stage 3.2 default-agent compatibility remains. Comparison uses a constant-time secret comparison. Tokens are not logged or returned in MCP errors. Expiry and external identity providers remain deferred.

docs.title: Configurable authentication modes
docs.text:
The canonical mcp.authentication configuration defaults to bearer, which preserves bearer-only operation. none resolves every request as the internal, non-persistent anonymous-mcp principal using the configured anonymous profile; a well-formed Bearer header is ignored for identity selection, while malformed or unsupported Authorization headers are rejected. mixed resolves a missing Authorization header as that anonymous principal and a valid Bearer header as its configured agent. An explicitly invalid or revoked Bearer is always rejected—PHOS never falls back to anonymous access after an invalid credential.

Anonymous access is enabled only when none or mixed is selected. It uses the existing standard or observer permission profile and does not create an agent record or credential. In mixed mode, revoking a bearer prevents use of that authenticated identity, but does not prevent a client from reconnecting without a token when anonymous access is enabled.

Mode Without token With valid Bearer token Bearer Rejected Registered authenticated agent None anonymous-mcp anonymous-mcp Mixed anonymous-mcp Registered authenticated agent

Bearer Token Only is the default. It resolves the registered agent identity and its configured permission profile; credentials can be rotated or revoked. No Authentication uses the shared anonymous-mcp principal, so callers are not individually identifiable through MCP authentication. Mixed permits both: a missing token selects the anonymous principal, while a valid token selects its registered agent. Explicitly invalid or revoked Bearer tokens are rejected and never fall back to anonymous access.

docs.title: Anonymous permissions
docs.text: Both anonymous profiles use the same PHOS authorization boundary as registered agents. observer is read-only. standard can use the semantic reads and currently exposed actions permitted to a standard agent, including supported expression, speech, sleep/wake, and user-signal requests, subject to runtime, capability, privacy, and safety checks. It may also access Resources available to the standard profile. Anonymous access never bypasses semantic arbitration or PHOS safety protections.

docs.title: MCP Authentication & Security
docs.text:
Configure authentication in Settings → MCP. Select Bearer Token Only, No Authentication, or Mixed Authentication. For No Authentication and Mixed, choose the anonymous Standard or Observer profile. Web Administration shows a security warning and requires explicit confirmation before enabling unauthenticated access.

The validated authentication policy is applied to new MCP HTTP requests without rebinding the listener or restarting PHOS. Clients affected by a mode change should reconnect. Requests already being processed retain the policy snapshot with which they started; PHOS does not claim targeted termination of SDK-owned transport sessions or subscriptions.

docs.title: Security considerations for unauthenticated MCP access
docs.text:
An endpoint without token enforcement can be used by any client that can reach it. With the Standard profile, an unintended caller may make PHOS speak, change expressions, request sleep or wake, trigger semantic signals, and read allowed environmental or presence-related context. This matters because PHOS is a physical robot.

HTTPS encrypts traffic; it does not authenticate callers. A public HTTPS tunnel can make a local MCP endpoint reachable from the Internet, and a URL is not an adequate access control. A tunnel or reverse proxy with its own enforced access restrictions is different from a publicly reachable tunnel, but PHOS still applies its configured MCP authentication and authorization.

Anonymous callers share one internal identity. PHOS cannot reliably distinguish anonymous applications, individual bearer revocation does not block anonymous access, and audit attribution is limited. Existing safety arbitration is not a substitute for authentication.

Recommended safeguards:

  1. Keep Bearer Token Only as the default.
  2. Enable anonymous access only when it is required.
  3. Restrict access at the tunnel, reverse proxy, or network boundary.
  4. Use Observer when actions are unnecessary; use Standard only when needed.
  5. Monitor unexpected MCP access and disable anonymous access when finished.
  6. Do not expose Web Administration or unrelated PHOS services through an MCP tunnel.

docs.title: Connecting Remote MCP Clients
docs.text:
PHOS exposes Streamable HTTP at its configured endpoint, for example http://<PHOS_IP>:8001/mcp. An HTTPS tunnel or reverse proxy can provide a remote endpoint such as https://example.ngrok-free.app/mcp; these URLs are illustrative. The tunnel provides connectivity, while PHOS performs configured authentication and permission checks.

External MCP Client → HTTPS tunnel / reverse proxy → PHOS MCP Server
                                                    → authentication + permissions
                                                    → AgentApplicationService
                                                    → PHOS semantic services

For a remote client, verify transport reachability, MCP initialization, tool discovery, Resource access, tool execution, and subscriptions separately. A successful connection alone does not prove every capability is available.

docs.title: Example: connecting an AI assistant through an HTTPS tunnel
docs.text:
ChatGPT is one example of a compatible MCP client; the same approach applies to other clients that support Streamable HTTP and the chosen authentication method.

  1. Enable the PHOS MCP listener.
  2. In Settings → MCP, select Mixed Authentication only if anonymous access is needed.
  3. Select the least-privileged anonymous profile for the use case.
  4. Configure an HTTPS tunnel to forward to the PHOS MCP port.
  5. Configure the client with the resulting URL ending in /mcp.
  6. Use its supported authentication option, connect, and verify tool discovery.
  7. Test a read-only operation before requesting an authorized action.

Not every MCP client supports unauthenticated Streamable HTTP, and client setup screens vary. In Bearer mode, supply an issued credential through the client's safe credential mechanism rather than a URL or command line.

docs.title: Troubleshooting remote access
docs.text:
• Confirm the URL ends in /mcp, the tunnel forwards to the correct PHOS host and port, and the MCP listener is running.
  • A Bearer-only endpoint rejects missing credentials. In Mixed mode, an invalid or revoked supplied Bearer is rejected; omit it only when anonymous access is intentionally enabled.
  • Check tunnel, reverse-proxy, and client protocol-header errors separately from PHOS MCP errors. A tunnel 502, timeout, or connection failure usually does not identify an MCP application problem.
  • Reconnect clients after authentication configuration changes.

docs.title: Credential lifecycle
docs.text:
AgentCredentialService is the application/service boundary for credential management surfaces:

create / rotate / revoke
→ AgentCredentialService
→ SecretsService
→ stable credential.secret_ref
→ BearerAgentAuthenticator

The service generates a URL/header-safe 256-bit bearer with the operating system CSPRNG. It returns a bearer only from creation or rotation, never via status or a read-back operation. Rotation replaces the value at the same secret_ref, immediately invalidating the old bearer; revocation removes the stored secret and leaves its configured AgentIdentity and permission profile intact. Authentication looks up the secret for each request, so no PHOS restart is needed. Expiry policies and external identity providers remain future work.

Authenticated Web Admin exposes agent create/edit/delete and this lifecycle at Settings → Agents. IDs are immutable; profile edits affect subsequent requests using the same bearer. It generates a valid non-secret reference only when a credential is created. The default agent cannot be deleted; deleting another agent confirms revocation first. Newly created or rotated bearers appear once in the immediate response and cannot be retrieved after navigation or reload. Rotation, revocation, and deletion require confirmation.

Agent creation, deletion, and permission-profile edits do not require a PHOS restart: new MCP authentication resolves the current registry. Already-open MCP sessions are not forcibly terminated and may retain their current request or session context; clients should establish a new request/session after a change. Selecting a different default agent also persists and publishes immediately; it changes only trusted-local/default compatibility resolution, never an explicitly authenticated agent identity. The selected default is protected from deletion until another configured agent becomes default.

docs.title: Permission profiles
docs.text: standard agents can use the complete currently exposed semantic tool set and the protected camera snapshot Resource/tool. observer agents retain read-only semantic context but cannot request control actions such as sleep, wake, speech, expression changes, or user signals; they also cannot read the camera snapshot. Permissions are enforced by PHOS on every authenticated request.

docs.title: Connecting a client
docs.text:
Use Streamable HTTP directly when the client supports it. For a local stdio connection from Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or an IDE, the recommended adapter is phos-mcp-bridge (Node.js 20+). It is maintained separately from the PHOS runtime. For a generic compatible client, connect to the configured endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp) and send an already-issued bearer through an HTTP Authorization header when credential mode is enabled. See Bridge authentication for the verified boundary and keep bearer values out of command lines.

For a network-accessible Pi, the bridge's upstream URL is http://<PHOS_IP>:8001/mcp, using the actual configured address. Configure the listener/network or a tunnel as described in remote clients; the committed listener still binds only to loopback.

docs.title: Physical tool calls and retries
docs.text: The bridge never automatically retries tools/call, including when an upstream transport fails. PHOS may have completed the physical action before the connection dropped. Future requests can establish a fresh session, but reconnection must not replay the uncertain action. Inspect current PHOS state before choosing whether to issue a new call.

docs.title: Bridge authentication
docs.text:
MCP Stage 3.6 completes authentication support in phos-mcp-bridge. It is a transport-only stdio bridge; it does not validate a credential or contain identity, permission, camera-permission, or resource-permission logic:

flowchart TD
  client[Claude / IDE / Inspector] <-->|MCP stdio| bridge[phos-mcp-bridge]
  token[PHOS_MCP_TOKEN environment] --> bridge
  bridge <-->|Streamable HTTP / Authorization bearer| phos[PHOS MCP server]
  phos --> auth[BearerAgentAuthenticator] --> identity[AgentIdentity]
  identity --> profile[PermissionProfile] --> service[AgentApplicationService]
  style bridge fill:#2e1065,stroke:#a855f7,color:#fff
  style phos fill:#1e293b,stroke:#8b5cf6,color:#fff

The bridge reads its already-issued bearer from PHOS_MCP_TOKEN and injects it only through its upstream Streamable HTTP transport. The bearer applies to initialization, tools, Resources, subscriptions, and reconnects. An absent or empty PHOS_MCP_TOKEN sends no Authorization header. A visible --token or visible --header Authorization argument is rejected: do not put a bearer in CLI arguments. Bearer values and Authorization headers are redacted from bridge logging and error paths.

PHOS remains authoritative for authentication, AgentIdentity resolution, PermissionProfile, authorization, camera permissions, and Resource permissions. Invalid or missing credentials fail at PHOS; the bridge does not retry as an unauthenticated or default identity. PHOS errors, including permission_denied, are preserved.

Obtain the bearer through the PHOS credential lifecycle/Web Admin, then launch the bridge without placing it on the command line:

export PHOS_MCP_TOKEN='...'

node /path/to/phos-mcp-bridge/dist/index.js \
  --url http://<phos-host>:8001/mcp

For Inspector TUI, the current working syntax is:

PHOS_MCP_TOKEN='...' \
npx --yes @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest --tui \
  --protocol-era modern \
  node /Users/francescoazzola/Documents/dev/phos-mcp-bridge/dist/index.js \
  -- \
  --url http://192.168.1.127:8001/mcp

The bridge does not manage the credential. If PHOS rotates or revokes it, the old bearer no longer authenticates. Update PHOS_MCP_TOKEN and restart or relaunch the bridge if required by its current implementation to establish a new authenticated upstream MCP connection. Hot credential reload is not claimed.

MCP exposes the existing AgentApplicationService, never hardware, renderers, camera/provider objects, controllers, or raw runtime state. Available tools are phos_get_status, phos_get_physical_context, phos_get_presence, phos_get_attention, phos_get_observed_expression, phos_get_camera_snapshot, phos_capture_camera_snapshot, phos_get_visible_objects, phos_set_expression(expression), phos_speak(text), phos_sleep, phos_wake, phos_signal_user(signal), phos_query_measurements(metric, start?, end?, limit?), and phos_list_physical_transitions(event_type?, limit?), phos_get_physical_assessment(), and phos_set_state(state, duration_ms?). Input bounds, permission checks, semantic result documents, and sanitized error mapping are transport-independent.

phos_set_state owns only a temporary, identity-scoped visual lease. It accepts thinking with a required integer duration_ms from 250 through 60000, or idle to release the caller's lease. duration_ms is optional for idle and is ignored when supplied. It requires control_visual_state; a lease expires automatically and never changes RobotCore.state. Core error, sleeping, speaking, and listening visuals retain priority. Its response uses the application result fields accepted, requested_state, effective_state, lease_active, remaining_expiry_ms, and suppressed_by; it exposes no other agent identity or lease data. This is distinct from the persistent REST state command. As an accepted MCP request, it participates in existing follow_agent arbitration: authenticated Agents may activate their assigned skin, while an anonymous request can use only the configured low-priority default-agent fallback.

docs.title: MCP Resources
docs.text: PHOS exposes read-only MCP Resources through the same permission-checked application-service boundary as its tools:

docs.title: Object awareness
docs.text:
phos_get_visible_objects takes no arguments and requires read_perception (not read_camera_snapshot). It performs one on-demand NanoDet observation from the already-running VisionPipeline's latest in-memory frame. It returns no image, box, identity, or tracking data:

{"captured_at":"2026-01-02T03:04:05Z","age_ms":25,"freshness":"fresh","objects":[{"label":"car","confidence":0.9}],"truncated":false}

Object awareness is disabled by default. Enabling it requires a locally installed NanoDet-m-plus-1.5x_416 FP32 ONNX model path; verify SHA-256 4b82da9944b88577175ee23a459dce2e26e6e4be573def65b1055dc2d9720186. The OpenCV Zoo asset is Apache-2.0. Requests may report unavailable for no/stale frame or disabled Vision, busy for an active inference, and timeout when the bounded on-demand request expires. No frames or detections are persisted.

Resource MIME type Purpose phos://status application/json Compact semantic robot status. phos://physical-context application/json Current Semantic Physical Context. phos://physical-context/assessment application/json Read-only bounded temporal evidence and source availability. phos://environment application/json Current environmental semantic context. phos://vision/snapshot image/jpeg Current on-demand camera snapshot.
  • phos://status — compact agent-facing semantic status.
  • phos://physical-context — provider-independent semantic physical context.
  • phos://physical-context/assessment — bounded retained-measurement evidence for supported environmental and air-quality metrics.
  • phos://environment — the environmental section of that physical context.
  • phos://vision/snapshot — one current image/jpeg camera snapshot.

phos_get_camera_snapshot returns a JPEG encoded from the same latest cached Vision frame as an MCP image content block, plus a small text block with captured_at (UTC), age_ms (monotonic-clock elapsed time), and freshness (fresh through 2 seconds, otherwise stale). captured_at is recorded when PHOS receives the frame from its camera provider; it is not the request or JPEG encoding time, and it is not a hardware exposure timestamp. Stale frames remain available but are never labelled current. The tool never initiates a capture, infers scene content, or changes presence/attention state. Tool calls are bounded to one snapshot per second per authenticated identity; the existing Resource remains available for its current read-only JPEG contract.

phos_capture_camera_snapshot has the same image, permission, JPEG-bound, and metadata format, but its metadata starts source=on_demand. PHOS records the current Vision frame sequence when the request is accepted and waits for a later frame from the already-running pipeline, for up to three seconds. It is not a separate sensor capture. The cached and on-demand tools share the same per-identity transfer limit, so alternating calls cannot bypass it; at most four on-demand waits may be pending. A timeout, stopped/restarted pipeline, or camera failure returns a sanitized error and never falls back to the preceding frame. Both camera paths reject JPEGs larger than 512 KiB.

Resources are live snapshots: each read calls the same permission-checked application-service boundary as the corresponding semantic tool. They do not poll providers, mutate PHOS, replay history, or expose controller/camera/ renderer internals. The camera snapshot is synchronous, read-only and encodes the existing Vision pipeline's latest cached frame; it never opens another camera, starts a capture, or streams video. It is protected by the dedicated read_camera_snapshot permission; the standard profile has it while the observer profile deliberately does not. This is separate from generic physical-context access because a snapshot may contain people physically visible to the camera. It contains no camera device, provider/backend, filesystem, identity, candidate-ID, debug, or EXIF/location metadata.

docs.title: Physical assessment evidence
docs.text:
phos://physical-context/assessment requires read_physical_history. It is a read-only assessment of the existing six-hour RAM-only measurement history and the current sensor snapshot; it neither polls a provider nor changes retained history. Each supported metric includes its retained sample count, first/last PHOS receipt timestamps, actual coverage, largest observed retained-sample gap, source provenance, and current source availability/age.

The assessment outcome is one of valid, stale, unavailable, insufficient_data, or unknown, with a stable machine-readable reason. insufficient_data is an expected evidence result, not a transport error: it means PHOS cannot safely establish enough retained coverage or continuity. Historical valid samples do not prove that a source is currently fresh.

PCI-01a intentionally provides no rising/falling/stable classification. The retained timestamp is PHOS receipt/recording time, not an asserted hardware acquisition time; metric-specific noise/deadband policy is required before numerical trend classification can be added. eCO2 remains an estimated air-quality measure, not direct CO2 concentration.

The metric-level evidence section always describes the full requested historical window. Its observed_discontinuity result is never silently removed after a sensor recovers. When a recorded unavailable-to-available transition has a reliably ordered timestamp, the additive recent_continuous_segment section separately describes only retained samples strictly after that recovery boundary. It may become valid after at least three samples, two minutes of coverage, no excessive retained gap, and no later recorded availability break, while the full historical outcome remains insufficient_data / availability_discontinuity.

Successful reconnect does not prove uninterrupted hardware acquisition. Equal or unordered PHOS receipt timestamps, missing recovery transitions, source changes, stale current data, or insufficient post-recovery samples keep the recent segment unknown or insufficient_data. The recovery boundary is a PHOS semantic-event receipt time, not an ESP32 acquisition timestamp or a hardware generation identifier.

docs.title: Discovery and snapshot read
docs.text:
The phos-mcp-bridge dynamically forwards MCP Resources, so no bridge-specific snapshot implementation is required. Set PHOS_MCP_TOKEN as described in Bridge authentication when PHOS uses bearer credentials. For a trusted-LAN PHOS endpoint:

npx --yes @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest --cli \
  node /Users/francescoazzola/Documents/dev/phos-mcp-bridge/dist/index.js \
  --url http://192.168.1.127:8001/mcp \
  --method resources/list

The result includes the four URIs in the table above. Read the current snapshot with the Inspector CLI syntax supported by the installed version, for example:

npx --yes @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest --cli \
  node /Users/francescoazzola/Documents/dev/phos-mcp-bridge/dist/index.js \
  --url http://192.168.1.127:8001/mcp \
  --method resources/read --uri phos://vision/snapshot

The response has MIME type image/jpeg and binary MCP Resource content. The Inspector may serialize that content as a textual blob representation for CLI output; PHOS itself does not use a JSON/base64 snapshot contract.

docs.title: Async resource-change subscriptions
docs.text:
Modern MCP clients negotiating protocol revision 2026-07-28 can use subscriptions/listen for phos://status, phos://physical-context, phos://physical-context/assessment, and phos://environment:

listen -> notifications/resources/updated -> resources/read

Notifications are URI-only change cues, not PHOS event payloads. Robot state maps to status and physical context; environmental condition maps to environment and physical context; air quality, motion, presence, attention, and observed expression map to physical context; capability and system-health changes map to status. phos://vision/snapshot is never announced because it is on-demand, not a video stream.

Numeric sensor samples remain read-only Resource data and do not cause push notifications. Confirmed environmental/motion conditions and meaningful sensor availability or freshness status transitions do cause Resource update cues. environment_availability_changed updates phos://environment, phos://physical-context, and the assessment Resource; air_quality_availability_changed also updates the assessment Resource. Environmental and air-quality condition transitions do the same. Numeric sensor samples still do not create push notifications, so clients use notifications as cues and reread the current Resource when appropriate. Camera snapshots remain excluded from continuous notifications.

The SDK owns listen-stream filtering, disconnect cleanup, and bounded per-client delivery. PHOS owns one bounded bridge subscription for its MCP listener and coalesces duplicate pending resource URIs. MCP subscriptions are not an event log: there is no replay, no history, and no raw sensor-telemetry push. Updates while disconnected are not replayed; reconnect, open a new listen stream, and read current Resources. In credential mode each subscription request is authenticated, but subscription authorization is deliberately cue-only: ResourceUpdated contains only a URI, and every subsequent resources/read authenticates and applies the resource permission again. A subscription therefore cannot disclose a protected camera frame to an observer. Presence changes (no_one / person_present) and semantic attention changes both update phos://physical-context. The re-read projection contains only anonymous presence state, count, and reliable confidence plus semantic attention state and non-identifying target coordinates/confidence; it never contains a candidate ID, target ID, face embedding, or camera frame. Delivery is best-effort: a notification says only that the Resource may have changed, not that a client acted on it or that every intermediate state was observed.

This is standard MCP Resource subscription support, not MCP Events and not a mechanism that independently activates any AI agent's reasoning. Compatible agents choose whether to subscribe and what to do after re-reading a Resource. The currently pinned Python MCP SDK provides subscriptions/listen but does not provide native typed MCP Events discovery or the events/list, events/subscribe, and events/unsubscribe methods. A future, optional, provider-neutral MCP Events adapter remains deferred until those native SDK extension points are available. It must be independently enabled and must not change the endpoint behavior seen by ordinary MCP clients. The separately owned phos-mcp-bridge has been externally validated for a long-lived stdio subscriptions/listen connection: two consecutive phos://status ResourceUpdated notifications were forwarded from PHOS Streamable HTTP to the Inspector. Bridge code is not owned or modified by this repository.

The bridge's Node 22 build and automated suite validate its standard MCP subscription forwarding path. Live physical interoperability remains a manual Raspberry Pi integration test.

docs.title: Raspberry Pi validation
docs.text:
systemctl --user restart phos.service
systemctl --user status phos.service --no-pager
ss -ltnp | grep 8001
journalctl --user -u phos.service -n 100 --no-pager

On the Pi, start the MCP Inspector with npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector. In its connection form select Streamable HTTP and enter http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp; connect, then call each available tool. From a workstation, first use an SSH tunnel and use the same Inspector URL locally:

ssh -N -L 8001:127.0.0.1:8001 pi@PHOS_HOST
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector

For an explicitly configured LAN host, connect only from that trusted LAN to http://LAN_ADDRESS:PORT/PATH; do not forward it to the Internet.

docs.title: Recorded physical validation
docs.text: Direct Streamable HTTP validation confirmed phos://status sleep/wake notifications, phos://physical-context semantic updates, and phos://environment availability updates. Sensor freshness validation confirmed environment loss/recovery and motion/IMU availability transitions. The bridge validation above confirmed a stdio subscription to phos://status and two consecutive ResourceUpdated notifications. These checks did not include physical air-quality validation. With Camera Preview disabled, phos://vision/snapshot remained available and resources/read returned an image/jpeg Resource with a non-empty blob. This validates resource availability and JPEG output only; it does not validate image content quality.

docs.title: Temporal History v0.1
docs.text: phos_query_measurements(metric, start?, end?, limit?) returns accepted RAM-only numeric observations and a min/max/average summary. start and end are timezone-aware RFC 3339 timestamps, the requested interval may not exceed six hours, and limit is 1–360. phos_list_physical_transitions(event_type?, limit?) returns confirmed semantic transitions with a 1–360 limit. Both require read_physical_history. History holds at most six hours, one sample per metric per minute, 360 samples per metric, and 500 transitions; it is lost on restart. Missing, stale, and unavailable inputs are not fabricated or interpolated. History excludes camera/audio data, transcripts, and identity.

docs.title: Physical Context Intelligence v0.1 — agent composition contract
docs.text:
PHOS supplies factual physical observations and bounded summaries. An external Agent combines those facts with its own task context and is solely responsible for interpretation and decisions. This is an on-demand composition pattern, not a PHOS runtime subsystem: it starts no worker, polls no sensor, or persists additional data. It exposes one read-only assessment tool and Resource over the existing bounded history.

Use phos_get_physical_context first to obtain the current semantic context. Its environment section reports status, available, temperature_c, pressure_hpa, humidity_percent, last_update, and age_seconds. Its air_quality section similarly reports status, available, eco2_ppm, tvoc_ppb, aqi_uba, last_update, and age_seconds. The same document includes current robot, presence, and attention sections. The current context establishes whether a reading is currently available or stale; history does not turn an unavailable sensor into a current one.

Use phos_get_physical_assessment before treating retained measurements as continuous evidence, especially after an interruption. It reports current source availability/freshness, historical-window evidence validity, and—when a recovery boundary is safely ordered—the validity of the recent post-recovery segment. It does not make current environmental conditions its primary answer, guarantee physical measurement accuracy, or detect rising/falling/stable trends. Use phos_get_physical_context for current perceived conditions, and combine phos_get_physical_assessment with phos_query_measurements for a time-window question.

Tool descriptions and read-only annotations guide MCP clients and Agents, but cannot guarantee that every Agent selects the appropriate tool.

For a selected time window, call the history tools with their actual signatures:

phos_get_physical_context()
phos_get_physical_assessment()
phos_query_measurements(metric, start?, end?, limit?)
phos_list_physical_transitions(event_type?, limit?)

For example, an Agent determines its own RFC 3339 UTC start timestamp for one hour ago, then requests:

phos_query_measurements("temperature_c", start="2026-11-19T09:00:00Z",
                        end="2026-11-19T10:00:00Z", limit=360)

The measurement result contains metric, samples, count, and summary. Each sample contains metric, value, unit, observed_at, source, and quality. When samples exist, summary contains minimum, maximum, average, delta, coverage, start, and end; start and end are the first and last returned samples. The delta is PHOS's arithmetic last-value minus first-value summary, not an interpretation of comfort, safety, or cause.

Use the same query for humidity_percent, pressure_hpa, eco2_ppm, tvoc_ppb, or aqi_uba. Query only the metrics relevant to the Agent's task; there is no combined trend endpoint. For the latest confirmed presence change, request:

phos_list_physical_transitions(event_type="presence_changed", limit=1)

For recent attention or robot-state changes, use event_type="attention_changed" or event_type="robot_state_changed", with a suitable limit. A transition result contains transitions and count; each transition contains type, current, previous, observed_at, and source.

docs.title: Observation and interpretation boundary
docs.text:
The following examples show the boundary deliberately:

Situation PHOS measurement or semantic observation PHOS mathematical summary External Agent interpretation Temperature rose in one requested hour Returned temperature_c samples have value 20.0 then 21.0. summary.delta is 1.0 with coverage: "sufficient". “Temperature increased by approximately 1 °C within the requested window.” Air-quality values changed Returned eco2_ppm, tvoc_ppb, or aqi_uba samples differ across the requested window. Each metric query returns its own min/max/average/delta. Describe the reported direction and magnitude; do not infer pollutant source or issue an autonomous response. Presence became present A presence_changed transition reports previous: "no_one" and current: "person_present". None. Transitions are semantic facts, not numerical trends. “PHOS last confirmed a presence-state change to person present at observed_at.” Trend cannot be established The metric has no samples, or one sample with summary.coverage: "insufficient" and summary.delta: null. No delta is supplied for one sample; no summary exists for zero samples. “There is insufficient retained measurement history to describe a trend.”

docs.title: Missing-data and retention contract
docs.text:
• No samples means PHOS has no retained observations for that metric and query; it does not mean the physical quantity was absent or unchanged.
  • One sample cannot establish a delta. Its summary has coverage: "insufficient" and delta: null; it must not be presented as a complete trend.
  • Two or more samples provide PHOS's coverage: "sufficient" summary, but do not guarantee continuous coverage of the requested interval. PHOS does not interpolate gaps.
  • phos_get_physical_context is authoritative for current sensor status, availability, and age. Stale or unavailable sensors must not be represented as fresh merely because retained samples exist.
  • No matching retained transition does not prove that no transition occurred. The requested event may predate retention, follow a restart, or not have been recorded by the active semantic source.
  • A presence transition is a confirmed semantic observation after PHOS's presence confirmation logic; it is not proof of a person's exact arrival or departure time.
  • All history is RAM-only, limited to the last six hours, and discarded on runtime restart.

This composition requires read_physical_history for both history tools and the physical-assessment Resource. phos_get_physical_context remains governed by read_physical_context; an Agent without history permission must not derive history from the current context.

docs.title: Motion awareness
docs.text: Motion is interpreted as a confirmed event, not treated as a direct renderer or GPIO command.

docs.title: Motion as semantics
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  sensor[MPU-6050] --> interpreter[MotionInterpreter]
  interpreter --> motion[MotionState / MotionEvent] --> behavior[BehaviorEngine]
  behavior --> output[Eyes]
  style behavior fill:#2e1065,stroke:#a855f7,color:#fff
  style interpreter fill:#1e293b,stroke:#8b5cf6,color:#fff
  style output fill:#1e293b,stroke:#8b5cf6,color:#fff

The optional GY-521/MPU-6050 service reads acceleration and angular velocity; it does not send raw values to the renderer or GPIO. MotionInterpreter turns fresh samples into confirmed semantic states: STILL, MOVING, TILT_LEFT, TILT_RIGHT, TILT_FORWARD, TILT_BACK, SHAKE and IMPACT.

docs.title: Visual reactions
docs.text:
• Directional tilt

    Tilt produces directional pupil intent and eye asymmetry.

  • Optional LED feedback

    The optional WS2812B ring is driven by the ESP32 through phos-hw v1 semantic LED commands. Its controller path is separate from eye-motion intent; it requires an active serial connection and advertised LED capability.

  • Shake & impact

    Shake and impact create short alert intent.

Temporary visual overrides

These reactions do not rewrite the configured base source. The currently resolved persistent visual state returns after the effect expires.

docs.title: Hardware validation
docs.text:
Check the physical installation

Check the board wiring and mounting axes, then verify the configured tilt directions and visual reactions on the Pi.

Details belong in the canonical hardware guide and architecture reference.

docs.title: PHOS 1.0.0 release record
docs.text: The current implemented capabilities are the complete 1.0.0 scope. The authoritative version is robot.__version__ in src/robot/__init__.py. Setuptools derives package metadata from it; startup logs and System / Status use that same value. Versioning is not runtime configuration.

docs.title: Included scope
docs.text:
• Raspberry Pi 3 runtime with an 800×600 animated face, independent render and Vision cadence, blink/gaze behavior, visual accents and state priority.
  • Layered, lightweight eye rendering with named cyan, blue, green, turquoise, amber, violet or white iris themes in canonical display configuration.
  • Local camera face selection/tracking and gaze; uncertain visible-expression observations mediated by BehaviorEngine, including abstention and decay.
  • Optional local-display camera picture-in-picture diagnostics, off by default, using the existing Vision camera owner and latest in-memory frame.
  • Explicit local ONNX or optional AWS Rekognition expression provider; cloud work is bounded, cached and rate-limited, without automatic provider fallback.
  • One canonical config/phos.json, strict startup/editor validation, config-relative paths and atomic saves. Deprecated explicit CLI overrides remain compatible; they never persist into the file.
  • Authenticated trusted-LAN web administration in its own process, with General, Network, Display & Appearance, Vision, Expression Recognition, Logging, Web Administration / Security and read-only System / Status pages.
  • Bootstrap password phos, mandatory rotation, salted password hashes outside configuration, expiring/revocable sessions, logout, CSRF and attempt limits.
  • Validated reload of logging level, eye appearance and camera preview through reusable runtime services, plus confirmed PHOS restart through a user systemd service; no OS reboot.
  • AWS credentials remain external in the SDK chain. There are no credential fields or credential values in configuration/status pages.

docs.title: Installation and operation
docs.text:
Use the installation guide for the exact supported source-deployment procedure and dependency snapshot. Start from the Pi's graphical desktop session:

cd /home/pi/phos
.venv/bin/python src/robot/main.py --config config/phos.json

The canonical defaults start only eyes. Set web.enabled true and web.host to the Pi's LAN address (or 0.0.0.0 for all IPv4 interfaces) to enable access. Open http://<PI-LAN-IP>:8080/, enter phos, change it to a different 12–256 character password, and log in again. Password recovery, per-domain editing, backup and HTTP limits are in the administration manual.

These examples are edits inside the existing complete configuration, not separate files. Preserve all other required fields:

{"expression": {"enabled": true, "provider": "local"}}

Local mode requires the model path, labels and preprocessing already configured under expression.local. Install/check the model from the installation guide. Face tracking without expressions uses vision.face_tracking_enabled: true and expression.enabled: false.

{"expression": {"enabled": true, "provider": "aws"}}

AWS mode uses expression.aws region/timeouts/limits and external credentials. It needs no local ONNX file; selected face crops leave the Pi. Set expression.enabled false to disable expression processing. Reload logging level, iris appearance or camera preview; restart for other configuration changes. Password changes take effect immediately.

docs.title: Hardening in this release
docs.text:
Camera configuration/start failures close the allocated camera. Camera closure is also attempted if stop fails. Partially started Vision and cancellation of startup release camera/core resources. Regression tests use fake hardware.

Source sync now stops on errors, creates deployment directories and copies the manual, packaging metadata and web dependency snapshot alongside the source. It still preserves deployed configuration, models and administrator data. Packaged installs carry the canonical JSON as data rather than recreating defaults.

docs.title: Verification and limits
docs.text:
Automated tests cover lifecycle rollback/cancellation, eye geometry and behavior, tracking, expression semantics, local/AWS selection using mocks, configuration validation/persistence, authentication, bootstrap rotation, CSRF, revocation, domain isolation, validated reload, restart confirmation and a real local web-worker socket/shutdown test. Detailed verification evidence and environment gaps are recorded in the implementation handoff.

The hardware record documents eyes/display and Pi Camera/tracking as operational. For deployment testing, run these checks on the target:

  1. Confirm Python imports, camera preview and the model checksum per installation.
  2. Run eyes-only and verify 800×600 output, animation cadence and Ctrl+C cleanup.
  3. Enable tracking; move/lose/reacquire a face and confirm smooth bounded gaze.
  4. Test local expressions with the actual model and verify happy/surprised observations, UNKNOWN abstention and neutral remaining disabled until calibrated.
  5. If AWS is used, verify credentials/region/permissions, bounded requests, connectivity failure and continued local eye/tracking behavior.
  6. Test first login, password change/logout, all domain pages from phone/tablet/ desktop, valid/invalid saves and restart application of saved settings.
  7. Install the user service; test logging-level reload, invalid reload rejection and confirmed browser restart with temporary web loss and changed network settings.
  8. Repeat start/stop, including SIGTERM, and check camera and port release plus Pi CPU/RAM use while logging in and running Vision.

Known limitations:

  • Expression accuracy has not been established; MobileFaceNet is the current configured candidate and FER+ a documented comparison/rollback. See model evaluation; no new accuracy claim is made.
  • HTTP is unencrypted and trusted-LAN-only. No TLS/public Internet deployment, multi-user administration or remote password reset is included.
  • Status reports parent-owned active configuration, not live health. AWS credentials are not probed. A crashed web worker requires PHOS restart.
  • Logging level, iris color and camera preview are reloadable; other configuration changes require restart; no automatic backup or cross-process file locking. Use one PHOS process per configuration/credential store.
  • Raspberry Pi OS/camera packages are installed by apt and are platform-specific; the Python web snapshot is pinned but this is not a byte-reproducible OS image.
  • Python 3.11+ is the documented release-installation baseline. The package's existing Python >=3.9 compatibility declaration is retained; older interpreters need compatible dependency resolution and are not the pinned release baseline.

There is no commit, release tag or publication implied by this release record. Post-1.0 work is explicitly deferred in the roadmap.

docs.title: PHOS 1.1.0 release record
docs.text:
Status: NOT READY — source release candidate; complete integration tests before tagging.

The authoritative version is robot.__version__ in src/robot/__init__.py, set to 1.1.0. Packaging, startup logging and Web Admin status derive from that single value. No commit, tag, deployment or publication is implied by this record.

docs.title: Scope actually implemented
docs.text:
