The read-only panel shows acceleration X/Y/Z in m/s² and angular velocity X/Y/Z in °/s, interpreted motion state, tilt direction, last event, timestamp, age and status. Factory scale only; no offset calibration means the adapter converted its ±2 g / ±250 °/s raw scale but did not require a motionless startup calibration. Values are hidden whenever unavailable or stale; the page never opens I2C itself. Setup and Pi verification are in the MPU-6050 installation guide.

IMU visual intensity and timing appear under Display & Appearance → Eye behavior. They are applied by Reload configuration. Persistent movement and tilt react while their motion state remains active; SHAKE and IMPACT use brief alert overlays followed by smooth decay. imu_tilt_eye_asymmetry_strength mirrors horizontal tilt eye sizes; impact strength must exceed shake strength so the strongest alert remains unambiguous. Robot states such as sleeping, speaking and error retain priority.

docs.title: Skin LED palettes (SKIN-03)
docs.text:
A skin may optionally carry an led_palette alongside its eye appearance. It is declarative theme metadata applied only through the existing runtime SemanticLedService. Configure this metadata directly in a skin YAML/package definition; Appearance → Skins does not edit palettes. Its Active LED Palette status reports the current runtime skin, palette state, semantic state, and available colors without creating a second palette selection or draft. Supported semantic states are idle, listening, thinking, speaking, sleeping, success, attention, and ambient. Omitted colors use the semantic LED fallback; catalog palettes may inherit parent colors. Warning and error remain protected system colors. The external-controller SemanticLedService remains the exclusive authority for intent, priority, animation, expiry, safety signals, and controller capability fallback.

The palette shape is {"enabled": true, "colors": {...}}. Colors must be canonical #RRGGBB values. Supported semantic keys are idle, listening, thinking, speaking, sleeping, success, attention, and ambient. warning and error are deliberately excluded: their safety colours remain arbiter-owned. A palette may be partial; omitted colors fall back to the arbiter's existing command colors. {"enabled": false, "colors": {}} explicitly disables a palette.

For catalog skins, an omitted led_palette inherits the parent palette; an enabled palette overlays only named colors; null removes an inherited palette; and a disabled palette stops inheritance. Built-in and custom skins without a palette are unchanged. Package exports now use manifest schema version 3 while imports remain compatible with schema version 2 packages. Read-only resolution follows the currently effective agent/default-agent skin, but no global LED settings are mutated.

The runtime supplies the resolved palette only after the corresponding visual appearance has been accepted. SemanticLedService then re-evaluates its current winner: a configured themeable color replaces that command's default color; missing/disabled/global palettes clear theme colors and use the existing command color; warning/error always use protected colors. This does not create, cancel, or extend an intent, so priorities, effects and expiries are unchanged. A controller reconnection still uses the existing arbiter reapply path, now with the current themed command. Read-only LED status includes palette metadata and whether the active color is palette, fallback, or protected.

docs.title: Authenticated MCP appearance activity
docs.text:
PHOS can retain per-agent appearance policy metadata: participation, priority, and an activity timeout. In appearance.mode: follow_agent, the runtime records an in-memory lease only after a registered agent has authenticated and completed an accepted MCP semantic tool or resource interaction. A successful MCP connection, transport keepalive, health check, anonymous request, invalid token, or permission-denied request does not renew a registered agent lease.

Leases use a monotonic clock and are never persisted. They expire after the agent's configured timeout, including when no new requests arrive. A restart therefore begins with no active leases. Eligible agents must participate and have an enabled, available assigned skin. The selector chooses the highest priority active eligible agent; equal priorities retain the previous winner while it remains eligible, otherwise their canonical IDs provide a stable tie break. The Default Agent does not affect this decision.

The arbitration result is lifecycle-owned and safe for later administration read models; it contains identities, selected skin IDs, priorities and lease state, never bearer values or secret references. Anonymous MCP clients retain their configured permissions and are never mapped to the default agent; when the explicit Appearance → Skins fallback is enabled they can select only its low-priority temporary skin candidate. Multiple authenticated sessions for one agent share one lease.

SKIN-02d.2 deliberately does not apply this result to the physical display. Existing manual Presentation Owner behavior remains unchanged; runtime visual activation is deferred to SKIN-02d.3.

docs.title: Website and documentation audit
docs.text: Audit basis: checked-out repository, MkDocs configuration, documentation, tracked assets, GitHub Actions workflows, configuration, MCP adapter, and tests reviewed during the 1.9.0 documentation redesign. This page records the documentation redesign findings.

docs.title: Current inventory and disposition
docs.text:
The following is the page-by-page disposition for every Markdown source page published by the MkDocs configuration. A move below means navigation placement; the source URL remains unchanged, so no redirect is needed.

Page Disposition Reason index.md UPDATE Reframe the entry page around physical interface, build, and agent paths. discover.md, features.md, how-phos-works.md, use-cases.md KEEP / MOVE Retain as Explore content; revise messaging where version or personality framing is inaccurate. vision-expressions.md, environmental-awareness.md, motion-awareness.md MOVE Keep specialist capability material under Explore. installation-overview.md, installation.md, hardware-overview.md, hardware.md KEEP / UPDATE Retain the canonical build/install/wiring detail; add a concise maker entry path. build-phos.md CREATE New evidence-bounded maker pathway; no invented BOM, price, or enclosure data. mcp-overview.md, mcp.md, ai.md, remote-api.md KEEP / UPDATE Separate the readable agent path from the exact MCP/REST reference. developer-quickstart.md CREATE New developer entry path using the verified Streamable HTTP boundary and bridge pattern. architecture.md, decisions.md, development.md, documentation.md KEEP Engineering and contributor references; configuration retains one canonical reference. vision.md, vision-model-evaluation.md, visual-system.md MOVE Retain under Reference; do not duplicate their implementation detail. voice.md, voice-commands.md, tts.md MOVE Retain under Reference; voice claims remain conditional on configuration/hardware. web-administration.md, web-admin-overview.md, hardware-controller.md, api.md, configuration-migration.md MOVE Retain operational and compatibility references. appearance/creating-skins.md MOVE Retain as optional customization, not primary product positioning. current-state.md, roadmap.md, releases.md, release-1.0.0.md, release-1.1.0.md, release-1.2.0.md, release-1.3.0.md, release-1.4.0.md, release-1.7.0.md, release-1.8.0.md, release-1.9.0.md KEEP / UPDATE Preserve technical history and publish the observed version discrepancy. contributing.md CREATE Surface issue reporting, maturity, and contribution-process decisions. website-audit.md CREATE Preserve the evidence, gap analysis, and URL/disposition decisions. Existing source URLs KEEP No source file moves were made; redirects are not required.

docs.title: Evidence-based gap analysis
docs.text: Requirement Existing page or implementation Current status Missing information Recommended change Priority Clear maker/developer entry paths Homepage, installation and MCP docs IMPLEMENTED None in documentation structure Keep Build and Developers as primary routes. High Current release version Git tag, robot.__version__, release test PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED Tag is 1.9.0; package/test are 1.8.0. Resolve source/tag metadata before publication. High Canonical YAML configuration RuntimeConfig, config/phos.yaml, migration guide IMPLEMENTED None identified Retain YAML-only wording and historical JSON context only. High Required/optional hardware Hardware/install docs and providers PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED Pi 4/5, BOM alternatives, prices, enclosure specs are unverified. State only the Pi 3/display baseline; obtain physical evidence before expanding. High MCP tool discovery MCP server and MCP reference IMPLEMENTED Client-specific setup is external to this repository. Keep the 17-tool/5-Resource reference canonical. High Authentic product media docs/assets/images/neon_phos_logo.png NOT IMPLEMENTED No verified reference-build photo/video is tracked. Obtain approved media with provenance and alt text. High License Repository root IMPLEMENTED Apache License 2.0, NOTICE, and a dependency audit are present. Confirm the copyright holder and complete release-specific third-party review before publication. Add a preferred discussion channel only after maintainer decision. Retain GitHub Pages-compatible MkDocs build. Regenerate branding derivatives when the source logo changes. Medium Simulator without hardware Tests use fakes/mocks UNKNOWN / NOT VERIFIED No end-user simulator is documented or verified. Do not promise one. Medium

docs.title: Navigation changes
docs.text: The previous Discover PHOS and broad Technical Documentation menus mixed audience goals with deep reference pages. The revised navigation uses Explore, Build PHOS, Developers, Reference, and Community. Technical pages remain at their original URLs and are not removed.

docs.title: Consistency findings
docs.text:
• The checked-out commit is tagged 1.9.0, while the Python package literal and release test report 1.8.0; the modified OpenAPI contract also reports 1.9.0. This is a release-management discrepancy outside this documentation-only change and must be resolved before publication.
  • YAML is the sole supported runtime configuration format. JSON remains used for API/MCP/controller payloads and may appear in historical material.
  • The MCP adapter exposes 17 named tools and five Resources in the checked-out implementation. External clients vary in Streamable HTTP and subscription support, so the site documents a compatible bridge pattern rather than promising support for every client.
  • The project license is Apache-2.0. The root NOTICE retains a [COPYRIGHT HOLDER] placeholder pending maintainer confirmation; this and the release-specific third-party audit remain publication prerequisites.

docs.title: Validation approach
docs.text: The documentation build is run with mkdocs build --strict. Link resolution and navigation are exercised by that build; physical hardware, external MCP clients, and social-preview rendering require the corresponding hardware/accounts and are reported separately rather than claimed as validated.

docs.title: Creating a Custom Skin
docs.text:
Build a portable .phos-skin package using the implemented version-3 manifest. This tutorial starts with the real Minimal built-in, creates an asset-free Copper pulse variant, validates it through PHOS, and installs it with Web Admin. It needs no camera, sensors, or LED hardware to display its eye styling.

For field-by-field rules, use the configuration reference. The structure guide describes package paths and limits.

docs.title: 1. Create a working directory
docs.text:
Run the following commands from the repository root with PHOS installed in its existing .venv. The directory is an authoring workspace, not a runtime plugin folder:

mkdir -p my-skin

docs.title: 2. Start from a real built-in
docs.text:
Write Minimal's actual exported manifest shape into your workspace. This uses PHOS's serializer; it does not change the running robot or its configuration.

PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
from robot.ui.skins import built_in_skins, skin_to_manifest

skin = next(item for item in built_in_skins() if item.id == "minimal")
manifest = skin_to_manifest(skin, skin.appearance)
Path("my-skin/skin.yaml").write_text(
    yaml.safe_dump(manifest, sort_keys=False), encoding="utf-8"
)
print("Wrote my-skin/skin.yaml")
PY

Alternatively, export Minimal from Appearance → Skins and extract its skin.yaml. An exported archive has the manifest at its root, without a parent folder and without image assets for this built-in.

docs.title: 3. Define metadata and visual properties
docs.text: Replace the workspace manifest with the complete example below. It selects an amber iris, an expressive eye contour, restrained amber State Effects, optional semantic LED colours, and calm idle timing.

docs.title: Complete manifest
docs.text:
schema_version: 3
name: Copper pulse
description: Warm irises and restrained effects, with calm idle timing.
appearance:
  eyes:
    iris_color: "#F4AB3D"
    shape: expressive
  backgrounds:
    enabled: false
    idle: null
    listening: null
    thinking: null
    speaking: null
    sleeping: null
    error: null
  eye_safe_layer:
    enabled: true
    mode: subtle
  state_effects:
    enabled: true
    preset: subtle
    palette: amber
    reduce_motion: true
led_palette:
  enabled: true
  colors:
    idle: "#F4AB3D"
    thinking: "#B38CFF"
    success: "#41CD7D"
physical_personality:
  preset: calm

led_palette is optional and has no physical effect without available controller-backed LEDs. Warning/error colours remain protected. Physical Personality is applied through effective-skin reconciliation, not through the live Preview button.

docs.title: Optional background assets
docs.text:
The complete example needs no assets. To add one:

  1. Create my-skin/assets/ and copy your own PNG/JPEG image there, for example idle.png.
  2. Set appearance.backgrounds.enabled: true and appearance.backgrounds.idle: assets/idle.png.
  3. Keep unassigned states null. For another state, use a separate filename, even when the image contents are identical.
  4. Prepare 800×600 images for the reference display. Check the package/image limits.

Put only referenced image files in assets/. Do not include the PHOS logo as an eye replacement; backgrounds are composed beneath the animated eyes.

docs.title: 4. Keep expressions and animations within supported controls
docs.text:
A skin chooses an eye shape and an effect preset/palette; it does not provide new expression profiles or animation scripts. Test expressions using the existing visual controls. State Effects follow the actual robot state, and Physical Personality changes bounded idle blink/gaze timing. reduce_motion applies to State Effects, not all eye motion.

Do not add arbitrary expressions, animations, geometry, or timing fields: they are not manifest extensions and will be rejected.

docs.title: 5. Validate the manifest
docs.text:
This invokes the same manifest validator used during package import without writing any PHOS state:

PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
from robot.ui.skins import skin_from_manifest

manifest = yaml.safe_load(Path("my-skin/skin.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
name, description, appearance, led_palette, personality = skin_from_manifest(manifest)
print(f"Valid manifest: {name}")
PY

docs.title: 6. Build and validate the archive
docs.text:
This command includes the manifest and immediate asset files, then performs a real package import into a temporary directory. Temporary validation does not activate the skin or edit your runtime configuration.

PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from zipfile import ZIP_DEFLATED, ZipFile
from robot.ui.skins import SkinRepository

workspace = Path("my-skin")
package = Path("copper-pulse.phos-skin")
with ZipFile(package, "w", compression=ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
    archive.write(workspace / "skin.yaml", "skin.yaml")
    assets = workspace / "assets"
    if assets.is_dir():
        for asset in sorted(assets.iterdir()):
            if not asset.is_file() or asset.is_symlink():
                raise ValueError("assets/ must contain only regular image files")
            archive.write(asset, f"assets/{asset.name}")

with TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
    repository = SkinRepository(Path(temporary) / "phos.yaml")
    installed = repository.import_package(package.read_bytes())
    assert repository.get(installed.id).name == "Copper pulse"
    print(f"Validated package: {package}")
PY

Keep the example name unchanged for the assertion, or update that assertion when authoring your own named skin. Manifest validation checks schema and parameters; package validation additionally checks paths, entries, sizes, asset references, and supported image signatures. Decoded-image limits require OpenCV/NumPy, as explained in Skin Structure.

docs.title: Other archive tools
docs.text:
For an image-backed package, the equivalent macOS/Linux commands are separate operations:

cd my-skin

COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 zip -X -r ../copper-pulse.phos-skin skin.yaml assets

For an asset-free package, omit assets:

zip -X ../copper-pulse.phos-skin skin.yaml

On Windows, select skin.yaml and assets/ themselves, not their parent folder, then create a ZIP archive and give it the .phos-skin extension. Exclude __MACOSX, .DS_Store, AppleDouble ._* files, and unrelated files.

docs.title: 7. Install and activate
docs.text:
1. Open Appearance → Skins in authenticated Web Admin.
  2. Import copper-pulse.phos-skin. It receives a new local custom ID.
  3. Choose Global Appearance if you want to assess this global selection without automatic active-agent changes.
  4. Use Preview for a temporary live visual check, then Apply to save it.
  5. Export the installed skin to keep a portable copy.

Apply uses the shared configuration/lifecycle boundary. Import alone does not change the appearance. See Installing and Activating for local catalogs, agent assignments, and restoring PHOS Default.

docs.title: 8. Test the result
docs.text:
• Verify the amber iris and expressive contour on the actual face display. Static SVG Preview currently uses the classic shape.
  • Exercise supported expressions; the skin must leave their semantic behavior and local state priorities intact.
  • Observe idle blink/gaze after Apply to assess the calm preset.
  • With supported hardware, inspect Active LED Palette and request only permitted signals; no LED hardware is needed for the eye appearance.
  • If using backgrounds, inspect each assigned state and confirm the eyes remain legible. Check centre-cropping on the target display.
  • Restart PHOS through your normal managed/foreground launch and confirm the saved global skin still resolves.

For errors or a difference between preview and the live display, use Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Skins
docs.text:
A PHOS skin is a reusable appearance definition for the physical interface your agents share. Choose iris colour and eye shape, state backgrounds, readability protection, visual effects, and an optional semantic LED palette. A skin can also select bounded idle blink and gaze timing through Physical Personality.

Skins make the same PHOS runtime recognisable in different settings or for different agents. They do not change an agent's model, reasoning, permissions, voice, or sensor interpretation.

docs.title: What a skin controls
docs.text: Part Customisation Boundary Eyes Canonical iris colour and one of five eye shapes Expressions, gaze intent, and blink events still come from the existing visual/behavior pipeline. Backgrounds Optional PNG/JPEG image for each of six robot states An image is selected by state; a skin does not create or change that state. Eye Safe Layer Enablement and halo strength Local contrast protection leaves the original background file unchanged. State Effects Enablement, intensity preset, palette, and reduced motion The engine supplies the state-specific animation; packages do not contain animation code. Semantic LEDs Optional colours for eight themeable intents Controller capability, arbitration, brightness, and animation timing remain runtime-owned; warning/error colours are protected. Physical Personality analytical, playful, or calm Changes low-priority idle blink/gaze timing, not conversational personality or safety/state priorities.

docs.title: Skins, expressions, states, and overlays
docs.text:
Skin describes the presentation. RobotState describes what PHOS is currently doing. FaceState carries resolved expression, gaze, blink, and visual intent to EyeRenderer.

A skin does not define new expressions or replace the animated eyes with an image. The existing expression profiles and robot-state priorities remain in force. Camera tracking, attention, and motion reactions can override idle gaze. Environmental markers, transient semantic notices, and protected Admin/recovery overlays remain separate from the skin package.

Global Appearance uses the saved global appearance. Follow Active Agent can temporarily select an eligible active agent's assigned skin. This is visual presentation arbitration, not a change of agent permissions or an agent orchestration framework. See installing and activating.

docs.title: Choose a path
docs.text:
• Built-in Skins: compare the three built-ins and shipped Aurora catalog entry.
  • Skin Architecture: discovery, rendering, activation, and fallbacks.
  • Skin Structure: packages, YAML catalogs, and managed storage.
  • Configuration Reference: fields, defaults, accepted values, and examples.
  • Creating a Custom Skin: build and validate a complete package.
  • Installing and Activating Skins: local files, Web Admin, runtime switching, and integration boundaries.
  • Troubleshooting: validation errors and current implementation limits.

Skins personalise PHOS's physical communication interface. Start with the visual system for expression semantics or Web Administration for the surrounding UI.

docs.title: Skin Architecture
docs.text: Skins reuse the existing appearance configuration, lifecycle services, render loop, and semantic LED arbitration. They are declarative data, not executable renderer plugins.

docs.title: Discovery and loading
docs.text:
SkinRepository combines three sources in order:

  1. Built-ins returned by built_in_skins().
  2. Optional YAML catalog selected by appearance.config_file, resolved beneath the active PHOS configuration directory.
  3. Managed custom skins persisted in skins.json beside that configuration.

The catalog resolves inheritance from another catalog entry or a built-in, merges partial appearance overrides, validates the resolved definition, and checks its referenced backgrounds. IDs must be unique across all sources. Cycles, unknown parents, excessive inheritance depth, invalid YAML/JSON, and conflicting IDs raise configuration errors; the list does not silently discard bad definitions.

Portable packages are imported into managed storage before appearing in this list. Import assigns a new custom-<uuid-hex> ID, rewrites background references, and saves metadata atomically. The package does not execute code or fetch assets from a URL. See structure and limits.

docs.title: From selection to a rendered frame
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  builtin[Built-in definitions] --> repository[SkinRepository]
  catalog[Optional YAML catalog] --> repository
  custom[Managed skins.json and assets] --> repository
  package[Imported skin package] --> custom
  repository --> services[Application and agent-management services]
  activity[Global mode or MCP agent activity] --> services
  services --> lifecycle[LifecycleService validation and reconciliation]
  lifecycle --> queue[Existing display-loop update queue]
  queue --> renderer[EyeRenderer and appearance resolvers]
  behavior[BehaviorEngine / FaceState] --> renderer
  renderer --> display[Tk display composition]
  lifecycle --> palette[SemanticLedService palette]
  palette --> controller[Optional controller LED output]
  • PhosApplicationService lists, imports, exports, previews, applies, and deletes skins through the shared application boundary.
  • AgentManagementService resolves global or selected-agent appearance and its Physical Personality/LED palette without persisting temporary ownership.
  • LifecycleService validates RuntimeConfig, applies supported visual changes, and reconciles the effective skin.
  • EyeRenderLoop queues appearance updates onto the existing display loop.
  • EyeRenderer consumes FaceState and validated iris/shape configuration. It interpolates visual targets while existing blink and expression logic run.
  • Background, Eye Safe, and State Effect resolvers select presentation for the effective state; they do not make behavior decisions.
  • SemanticLedService uses eligible theme colours while preserving runtime priority, animation parameters, controller availability, and protected colours.

docs.title: Display composition
docs.text:
The Tk adapter composes the existing layers in this order:

  1. State background.
  2. Eye Safe Layer.
  3. State Effects.
  4. Animated eyes.
  5. Environmental decorations.
  6. Optional local camera preview.
  7. Transient semantic notice.
  8. Protected local Admin/recovery overlay.

Backgrounds are prepared and cached for a path/display-size combination. The image is proportionally scaled to fill the display and centre-cropped; it is not stretched. Decode failure falls back to the renderer's background and is logged. Skin packages cannot replace the protected overlays or assign arbitrary drawing code to these layers.

docs.title: Preview, apply, and active-agent selection
docs.text:
Live Preview applies the four appearance blocks temporarily without saving or replacing the active configuration snapshot. It does not apply the skin's LED palette or Physical Personality. It has no automatic expiry timer; a later appearance application, reconciliation, or restart can replace it.

Apply builds and validates a complete configuration, saves appearance fields and appearance.global_skin_id, then requests reload. On failure the application attempts to restore the previous saved configuration. This is not a guarantee that every already-applied live subsystem change is rolled back; inspect runtime status after a failure.

Automatic reconciliation resolves the persisted global skin or the eligible active agent's assigned skin, applies visual settings through lifecycle, then applies Physical Personality and the effective LED palette. Unchanged resolved appearance is not repeatedly reapplied.

In follow_agent mode, accepted semantic MCP work renews the registered identity's activity lease. Authentication alone, denied work, and transport keepalives do not renew it. The highest-priority eligible active agent wins. On a tie PHOS retains the previous winner if possible; otherwise it selects a stable agent-ID order. Expiry returns selection to another eligible agent or the global fallback. This does not grant exclusive ownership of physical outputs.

docs.title: Fallback and failure handling
docs.text:
• Missing managed custom backgrounds are reported by state. Explicit live Preview/Apply can omit those assignments while retaining the stored skin.
  • Automatic selection of a skin with missing backgrounds falls back to global appearance rather than partially applying that agent skin.
  • An unavailable persisted global skin retains the saved display configuration and uses analytical Physical Personality.
  • Omitted eye shape resolves to classic_oval; omitted Physical Personality resolves to analytical during reconciliation.
  • Missing, disabled, or partial LED palettes use canonical fallback colours for unprovided intents; warning/error retain protected colours.
  • Missing runtime appliers reject live activation. Corrupt catalogs or custom metadata can make the catalog unavailable until repaired.

The troubleshooting guide distinguishes these designed fallbacks from current importer, snapshot, and static-preview limitations.

docs.title: Built-in Skins
docs.text:
PHOS defines three built-in skins in robot.ui.skins.built_in_skins(). They require no skin directory or background images and cannot be deleted or edited as built-ins. Export one to create an independent custom package.

The repository also supplies Aurora through config/skins.yaml. It is a catalog skin, not a fourth code-defined built-in; it appears when that catalog is configured and available.

docs.title: Compare the supplied appearances
docs.text:
Name / ID Iris and shape Eye Safe Layer State Effects Physical Personality PHOS Default / phos-default Cyan #28CEEB; classic_oval Enabled, balanced Disabled; balanced, phos, reduced motion off Omitted; effective fallback analytical Minimal / minimal White #DAECF6; classic_oval Enabled, subtle Disabled; balanced, phos, reduced motion off Omitted; effective fallback analytical Ambient / ambient Violet #A670F5; classic_oval Enabled, balanced Enabled; balanced, aqua, reduced motion off Omitted; effective fallback analytical Aurora / aurora Custom violet #B38CFF; inherited classic_oval Inherited enabled, balanced Inherited disabled; balanced, phos, reduced motion off Explicit calm

All four have backgrounds disabled and all six background assignments null. With no usable background image, the Eye Safe Layer has no image to analyse and does not add a halo. Minimal reduces visual complexity; it does not enable the State Effects reduced-motion option or disable normal blinking.

docs.title: PHOS Default
docs.text: “The standard PHOS appearance.” Cyan irises and the classic oval profile retain the baseline appearance. There is no skin LED palette, so semantic LED colours fall back to the runtime defaults.

docs.title: Minimal
docs.text: “Reduced visual complexity.” White irises and the subtle Eye Safe Layer setting provide an alternative baseline without backgrounds or State Effects. There is no skin LED palette.

docs.title: Ambient
docs.text:
“A calm PHOS effect palette.” Violet irises and enabled aqua State Effects add the built-in state treatments. The description refers to its visual palette; Ambient does not select the calm Physical Personality preset.

Ambient also supplies these optional semantic LED colours:

Intent Colour idle #38BDF8 listening #22D3EE thinking #818CF8 speaking #60A5FA sleeping #1E3A8A ambient #F59E0B

success and attention are omitted and use runtime fallback colours. Warning and error are not themeable. An active, LED-capable controller is required for physical LED output; selecting Ambient alone does not enable hardware.

docs.title: Aurora: the supplied catalog example
docs.text:
Aurora inherits phos-default, replaces only its iris colour, and selects calm idle timing. The complete shipped entry is shown in Skin Structure.

These images are static 800×600 neutral/idle SVGs generated through PHOS's existing render_preview function. They are not recordings of animation and do not illustrate Physical Personality timing. Use the running face display to assess transitions and idle behavior.

docs.title: Customise a supplied skin
docs.text: Use Appearance → Skins → Export, edit the exported package, and import it as a new custom skin. Package fields and accepted values are listed in the configuration reference. For Aurora, edit or inherit its catalog entry instead; the Web Admin does not provide an editor for catalog YAML. Follow Creating a Custom Skin for a complete working example.

docs.title: Skin Configuration Reference
docs.text: Portable manifests, local catalogs, and runtime selection are separate schemas. A package must supply its required fields; the baseline column below describes PHOS Default, not values the importer inserts for missing required fields. Only eye shape and the explicitly optional blocks have omission behavior.

docs.title: Portable manifest metadata
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default / accepted values Example schema_version Integer Yes No default; 3 for new packages; legacy 2 without version-3 optional blocks is accepted 3 name String Yes No default; use a nonempty name, at most 80 characters, for persistent custom records Copper pulse description String Yes No default; empty allowed; at most 240 characters for persistent custom records Warm irises and restrained effects. appearance Mapping Yes Exactly the four blocks below See the complete tutorial. led_palette Mapping or null No Omitted/null: no skin palette See semantic LEDs. physical_personality Mapping or null No Omitted/null: no skin preset; reconciliation falls back to analytical {preset: calm}

Metadata lengths are checked when managed custom records are loaded; use the limits above even though initial package-manifest validation checks only their string types. Packages do not accept id, inherits, or display_name.

docs.title: Appearance fields
docs.text: Every package includes eyes, backgrounds, eye_safe_layer, and state_effects beneath appearance, even when a feature is disabled.

docs.title: Eyes
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required PHOS Default / omission Accepted values Example appearance.eyes.iris_color String Yes #28CEEB; no omission default #RRGGBB or the named presets below; normalized to uppercase hex "#F4AB3D" appearance.eyes.shape String No classic_oval classic_oval, round, expressive, angular, compact expressive Iris preset Canonical colour cyan #28CEEB blue #4985FF green #41CD7D turquoise #23C8AF amber #F4AB3D violet #A670F5 white #DAECF6

Quote hex colours in YAML so # is not parsed as a comment. Iris colours do not accept alpha, gradients, texture paths, or animation definitions. Semantic eye-body accents remain controlled by the existing expression/state pipeline; the selected iris is not a replacement colour for every pixel.

Shape Renderer treatment classic_oval Existing oval rendering profile. round Circular open-eye geometry. expressive Custom contour with lifted outer corners. angular Winged contour with a tapered inner point. compact Reduced vertical radius and compact contour.

Packages cannot set pixel positions, eye dimensions, custom meshes, expression profiles, or arbitrary blink/gaze curves. These five shapes are the supported geometry choices. Validate custom shapes on the live display; the static SVG preview does not currently pass the selected shape to its renderer.

docs.title: State backgrounds
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required PHOS Default Accepted values Example appearance.backgrounds.enabled Boolean Yes false true, false true appearance.backgrounds.idle String or null Yes null Referenced package image or null assets/idle.png appearance.backgrounds.listening String or null Yes null Referenced package image or null assets/listening.jpg appearance.backgrounds.thinking String or null Yes null Referenced package image or null assets/thinking.png appearance.backgrounds.speaking String or null Yes null Referenced package image or null assets/speaking.png appearance.backgrounds.sleeping String or null Yes null Referenced package image or null assets/sleeping.png appearance.backgrounds.error String or null Yes null Referenced package image or null assets/error.png

Disabled backgrounds retain their assignments in the skin. Any non-null package reference still needs its asset in the archive. Use distinct filenames per assigned state because of the current importer limitation. See structure and image limits.

docs.title: Eye Safe Layer
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required PHOS Default Accepted values Example appearance.eye_safe_layer.enabled Boolean Yes true true, false true appearance.eye_safe_layer.mode String Yes balanced subtle, balanced, expressive subtle

The layer analyses usable background images and adds bounded local contrast protection. With no background or a sufficiently dark, low-variation image, it can draw no halo even when enabled. It does not modify the image file.

docs.title: State Effects
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required PHOS Default Accepted values Example appearance.state_effects.enabled Boolean Yes false true, false true appearance.state_effects.preset String Yes balanced subtle, balanced, expressive subtle appearance.state_effects.palette String Yes phos phos, cyan, blue, violet, aqua, amber, white, green amber appearance.state_effects.reduce_motion Boolean Yes false true, false true

All four fields remain required when disabled. The engine selects ambient, inward, circulating, outward, breathing, or restrained-error treatments by robot state. Presets scale their visual strength. Reduced motion limits State Effects speed, motion, and pulsing; it does not disable eye blinking, camera tracking, or every motion-related behavior.

docs.title: Semantic LED palette
docs.text:
This optional version-3 block sits beside appearance, not inside it:

led_palette:
  enabled: true
  colors:
    idle: "#F4AB3D"
    thinking: "#B38CFF"
    success: "#41CD7D"
Parameter Type Required Default / accepted values Example led_palette.enabled Boolean When the mapping is supplied true or false; no inserted default true led_palette.colors Mapping When the mapping is supplied May be empty or partial; disabled palettes must use {} {idle: "#F4AB3D"} led_palette.colors.idle Hex string No Omitted: runtime fallback "#F4AB3D" led_palette.colors.listening Hex string No Omitted: runtime fallback "#22D3EE" led_palette.colors.thinking Hex string No Omitted: runtime fallback "#B38CFF" led_palette.colors.speaking Hex string No Omitted: runtime fallback "#60A5FA" led_palette.colors.sleeping Hex string No Omitted: runtime fallback "#1E3A8A" led_palette.colors.success Hex string No Omitted: runtime fallback "#41CD7D" led_palette.colors.attention Hex string No Omitted: runtime fallback "#F4AB3D" led_palette.colors.ambient Hex string No Omitted: runtime fallback "#F59E0B"

LED colours require exactly #RRGGBB; iris preset names are not accepted here. Warning/error keys are rejected. Skins cannot change LED brightness, animation, priority, duration, hardware pins, or controller capability. A disabled palette is {enabled: false, colors: {}}; it disables the skin override, not the LEDs.

docs.title: Physical Personality
docs.text:
physical_personality:
  preset: calm
Parameter Type Required Default / accepted values Example physical_personality.preset String When the mapping is supplied analytical, playful, calm; absent block falls back to analytical calm Preset Idle timing policy analytical Blink interval 4.8–7.2 s; gaze rest interval 4.0–7.0 s. playful Blink interval 2.4–4.2 s; gaze rest interval 1.5–3.2 s; larger set of idle gaze offsets and more frequent double blinks. calm Blink interval 5.5–8.0 s; gaze rest interval 4.8–8.0 s; restrained idle offsets.

These are policy ranges, not guaranteed measured frame timings. The preset also selects double-blink pause/chance and gaze-hold ranges internally; skins cannot supply custom timing numbers. Attention, tracking, IMU reactions, and system states retain authority. Physical Personality belongs to the skin, not an agent's reasoning persona.

docs.title: Local YAML catalog
docs.text:
See the actual Aurora file for a complete example.

Parameter Type Required Default / accepted values Example schema_version Integer Yes Exactly 1 for catalogs 1 skins List Yes List of entries; empty allowed [] skins[].id String Yes Lowercase [a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}; unique across all sources copper-pulse skins[].display_name String Yes Nonempty after trimming, at most 80 characters Copper pulse skins[].inherits String or null Yes Built-in/catalog ID; null selects phos-default minimal skins[].appearance Mapping Yes Partial recursive overrides; {} retains the parent appearance {eyes: {iris_color: "#F4AB3D"}} skins[].led_palette Mapping or null No Omitted: inherit; null: clear; disabled: stop inheritance; enabled partial: merge colours {enabled: true, colors: {idle: "#F4AB3D"}} skins[].physical_personality Mapping or null No Omitted: inherit; null: clear; mapping uses a supported preset {preset: calm}

Catalog backgrounds use backgrounds/<filename> or managed custom-skin paths, not assets/. Unknown catalog fields, including package-style description, are rejected. Catalog definitions do not use the portable package schema.

docs.title: Runtime selection and per-agent policy
docs.text:
These fields belong to the existing full config/phos.yaml model, not skin.yaml. Merge changes into the active configuration; do not replace the entire runtime document with a skin manifest.

Parameter Type Default / accepted values Example appearance.config_file Path or null Shipped skins.yaml; older configurations default to null. Catalog must be a .yaml/.yml file beneath the active configuration directory. skins.yaml appearance.mode String global; accepts global, follow_agent follow_agent appearance.global_skin_id String or null null; nonempty ID when supplied phos-default appearance.anonymous_mcp_use_default_agent_skin Boolean false false appearance.presentation_owner.agent_id String or null null; retained legacy owner metadata; does not override automatic mode arbitration null agents.entries[].skin.enabled Boolean Both assignment fields required when skin exists; no assignment by default true agents.entries[].skin.id String or null Required with skin; nonempty known ID when enabled minimal agents.entries[].appearance.participate Boolean true when policy omitted true agents.entries[].appearance.priority Integer 50; range 0–100 60 agents.entries[].appearance.activity_timeout_seconds Integer 30; range 5–3600 45

The appearance policy mapping, when supplied, requires all three fields. Anonymous MCP fallback uses the default agent's eligible skin at fixed priority −1 with a 30-second lease, below authenticated candidates. It does not create a registered anonymous agent or grant that default agent's permissions.

Apply supported runtime settings through the existing lifecycle or Web Admin workflow described in Installing and Activating.

docs.title: Installing and Activating Skins
docs.text: Skin management uses the existing PHOS application and lifecycle services. The local runtime is required for live appearance; package import alone does not start it or change the display.

docs.title: Web Administration
docs.text:
Open Appearance → Skins after signing in.

Operation Result Import Skin Package Accepts .phos-skin or compatible .zip; validates and installs a new custom ID. Standalone YAML is not an upload format. Preview Temporarily applies eye/background/Eye Safe/State Effect settings live; does not save configuration or apply LED/personality settings. Apply Saves the skin's appearance and global ID, then requests runtime reload/reconciliation. Export Downloads a version-3 .phos-skin archive with referenced background files. Delete Skin Deletes a managed custom definition and owned assets, subject to reference checks; built-ins and catalog entries are not deleted through this action. Save mode Persists Global Appearance or Follow Active Agent and requests reconciliation.

The current card UI offers Preview, Apply, Export, and eligible custom-skin deletion. There is no card editor for YAML, renaming, LED palette editing, or Physical Personality editing. Edit an exported package and import it again. Repeated imports create distinct IDs rather than updating a previous skin.

Preview has no countdown or automatic revert. Apply a different appearance, trigger normal reconciliation, or restart to replace it. After Apply, verify runtime status; saving and the currently effective agent appearance are distinct.

docs.title: Manual local catalog
docs.text:
For a stable, source-controlled ID, use the supported catalog rather than copying arbitrary skin folders into the runtime.

  1. Place a catalog such as the repository's config/skins.yaml beneath the active configuration directory. Keep the three required entry fields plus appearance and any supported optional blocks.
  2. Put referenced background files under that directory's backgrounds/.
  3. Set appearance.config_file in the existing full runtime configuration.
  4. Select the catalog skin in Web Admin and use Apply. For manual selection, merge the following appearance section into the full configuration and restart through the normal deployment workflow.
appearance:
  config_file: skins.yaml
  mode: global
  global_skin_id: aurora
  anonymous_mcp_use_default_agent_skin: false
  presentation_owner:
    agent_id: null

This example selects the real shipped Aurora definition. Preserve unrelated runtime fields and agent records. Canonical model validation checks the runtime configuration; SkinRepository.list() checks the catalog itself. Changing a catalog file is not a filesystem-watched hot reload; request an explicit apply, reconciliation, or restart after edits.

The current Python wheel packages config/phos.yaml, but does not bundle config/skins.yaml. Source checkouts include it. When using an installed package without that catalog, copy the repository catalog alongside your active configuration, or set appearance.config_file: null to use only built-ins and managed custom skins. Do not leave a configured catalog path pointing at a missing file.

Portable-package manual installation is supported through the internal SkinRepository.import_package(bytes) boundary, as demonstrated in the tutorial's temporary validation. There is no dedicated skin-management CLI. Do not hand-create custom IDs or write skins.json as an installation shortcut.

docs.title: Runtime switching and per-agent appearance
docs.text:
Global Appearance uses the persisted global skin, falling back to saved display settings when there is no usable global definition.

For Follow Active Agent:

  1. In Settings → Agents, assign a known skin to the desired registered agent.
  2. Enable its appearance participation and choose priority/timeout.
  3. In Appearance → Skins, select Follow Active Agent and save the mode.
  4. Use the agent's normal MCP credential and perform accepted semantic work. The activity tracker renews that agent's appearance lease.
  5. Inspect current activation and Active LED Palette. On expiry, PHOS selects another eligible active agent or the global fallback.

Defaults are participation enabled, priority 50, and a 30-second activity window. Higher priority wins; existing winners are retained on a tie where possible. The complete ranges and optional anonymous default-agent fallback are in the configuration reference. A configured legacy presentation owner does not override this mode authority.

These appearance leases are distinct from phos_set_state's bounded thinking visual lease. Assigning a skin does not change permissions or give an agent exclusive access to the display. The global configuration is not overwritten by a temporary selected-agent skin.

docs.title: REST, MCP, and internal application boundaries
docs.text:
Surface Implemented appearance access Authenticated Web Admin /appearance/skins Package import, temporary preview, apply, export, deletion, and mode controls through application services. Web Admin GET /appearance/skins/<skin_id>/export Download a portable package; requires normal Admin access. Web Admin GET /appearance/preview.svg and /appearance/preview Static SVG and its preview page; not a live skin-activation API. Current shape/catalog limitations are documented under troubleshooting. REST /api/v1/config Existing authenticated full-configuration read/update boundary; not a skin package/catalog CRUD API. REST /api/v1/backgrounds/assets, /api/v1/backgrounds Existing managed background listing/configuration; not skin package import/export. MCP No skin-list/import/apply tool or skin resource. Accepted agent activity can indirectly select an administrator-assigned skin in follow_agent mode. Python application services Internal skin list/create/import/export/preview/apply/delete operations; these are not automatically public REST/MCP methods.

MCP expression, speech, signal, and thinking-state tools continue to use their existing permissions. They do not accept a skin manifest or choose arbitrary skin IDs. Follow the existing Remote API and MCP reference for those contracts.

docs.title: Restore PHOS Default
docs.text:
1. Select Global Appearance and save the mode if automatic selection is active.
  2. Find PHOS Default in Available Skins and choose Apply.
  3. Verify cyan irises, classic oval eyes, no assigned backgrounds, and disabled State Effects. Normal robot state and expressions still affect appearance.

This resets the appearance baseline; it does not reset sensors, credentials, agent records, or runtime behavior configuration. global_skin_id: null alone means “use saved global display values,” not “reset to PHOS Default.”

Before deleting a custom skin, remove or replace agent assignments, including retained disabled assignments, and apply another appearance if its owned backgrounds are still in use. Export a backup before deletion.

docs.title: Skin Structure
docs.text: PHOS has two authoring formats: a portable skin package and a local YAML catalog. Their schema versions and asset paths are different. Neither format contains Python, JavaScript, fonts, shaders, or executable plugins.

docs.title: Portable package
docs.text:
.phos-skin is a ZIP-compatible archive; Web Admin also accepts .zip. skin.yaml must be at the root. assets/ is optional and may contain only referenced PNG/JPG/JPEG files directly inside it.

copper-pulse.phos-skin
├── skin.yaml             # Required UTF-8 YAML manifest, schema version 3
└── assets/               # Optional; omit for a background-free skin
    ├── idle.png          # Referenced as assets/idle.png
    └── listening.jpg     # Referenced as assets/listening.jpg

This is the package layout used by the existing exporter/importer. There is no required directory per built-in skin: the built-ins are data definitions in src/robot/ui/skins.py. Exporting the real minimal built-in produces this complete archive, with no assets:

minimal.phos-skin
└── skin.yaml             # Minimal's full appearance, exported as schema version 3

docs.title: Manifest and filenames
docs.text:
• Required metadata: schema_version, name, description, and appearance.
  • Required appearance blocks: eyes, backgrounds, eye_safe_layer, and state_effects. Unknown blocks and parameters are rejected.
  • Optional version-3 blocks: led_palette and physical_personality.
  • No package ID: import always creates a new local custom ID.
  • Asset names start with an ASCII letter or digit, followed by letters, digits, dots, underscores, spaces, or hyphens, and end in .png, .jpg, or .jpeg.
  • No nested asset directories, absolute paths, backslashes, .. segments, symlinks, duplicate ZIP entries, or unreferenced files.
  • The exact assets/ directory entry may be present or omitted. Other directory entries, including a parent skin folder or __MACOSX/, are rejected.

The manifest validator accepts legacy version 2 without the version-3 optional blocks. New exports use version 3. The internal version-1 YAML import helper is not the public Web Admin upload format.

docs.title: Package and image limits
docs.text:
Limit Value Archive size At most 32 MiB Total declared unpacked size At most 32 MiB Entry count, including manifest/directory entries At most 16 Individual entry, including manifest At most 4 MiB Individual background image At most 4 MiB Decoded image dimensions when OpenCV/NumPy are available Width ≤1920 and height ≤1080

The importer checks file signatures and PNG/JPEG extension consistency. It performs decoded-image checks when OpenCV and NumPy are available; without them that decoding/dimension check is skipped. Prepare and validate images on the normal Pi installation with OpenCV. For the reference display, 800×600 images avoid aspect-ratio cropping.

The current importer writes each state's background separately with exclusive file creation. Use a distinct filename for each assigned state, even when images have identical contents. Reusing one filename across states currently fails import; it is not a supported packaging shortcut.

docs.title: The shipped catalog
docs.text:
The real repository layout is:

config/
├── phos.yaml             # Canonical runtime configuration; appearance.config_file: skins.yaml
└── skins.yaml            # Catalog schema 1; contains the Aurora definition
src/robot/ui/
└── skins.py              # PHOS Default, Minimal, Ambient, repository and validators

The complete config/skins.yaml is:

schema_version: 1
skins:
  - id: aurora
    display_name: Aurora
    inherits: phos-default
    physical_personality:
      preset: calm
    appearance:
      eyes:
        iris_color: "#B38CFF"

Catalog entries use stable lowercase IDs and may inherit another catalog entry or a built-in. inherits: null uses phos-default. Appearance dictionaries merge recursively; lists/scalars replace their parent values. Catalog LED palettes can inherit and override individual colours. Inheritance cycles, unknown parents, depth beyond eight, and IDs conflicting with other sources are rejected.

Catalog backgrounds use managed configuration-relative paths such as backgrounds/idle.png, not package-relative assets/idle.png. Referenced catalog images must already exist beneath the configuration directory's backgrounds/.

docs.title: Managed installation storage
docs.text:
Import/create operations write relative to the active configuration file, not necessarily the repository's config/ directory:

<active-configuration-directory>/
├── phos.yaml
├── skins.yaml                       # Optional configured catalog
├── skins.json                       # Managed custom metadata; written atomically
└── backgrounds/
    └── skins/
        └── custom-<uuid-hex>/        # Generated local ID, not an author-chosen name
            ├── idle.png
            └── listening.jpg

Use package import/export rather than manually editing skins.json. Import rewrites assets/... paths into this namespace; export rewrites them back and bundles referenced images. Store no credentials, transcripts, or runtime state in skin metadata.

docs.title: Skin Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the exact error, the active configuration directory, and whether the operation was Import, live Preview, Apply, or static SVG Preview. These paths have different validation and persistence behavior. Keep an exported package before editing managed files.

docs.title: Discovery and catalog errors
docs.text: Symptom Cause / action A folder is not listed as a skin PHOS discovers built-ins, the configured YAML catalog, and managed skins.json; it does not scan arbitrary skin directories. Import a package or add a catalog entry. Configured catalog is missing Resolve appearance.config_file relative to the active configuration file; copy the catalog there, or use null to disable that source. The current wheel does not include the repository catalog. Catalog has unsupported fields Use catalog schema 1 and required id, display_name, inherits, appearance; package fields are a different schema. Duplicate/conflicting ID Choose a unique lowercase catalog ID. Imported IDs are generated; do not replace built-in IDs or edit custom IDs by hand. Unknown parent, cycle, or depth error Inherit from an available built-in/catalog entry; remove cycles and keep inheritance within the eight-depth bound. Catalog background unavailable Place the referenced file beneath the active configuration directory's backgrounds/; catalog loading rejects missing references. Entire custom list unavailable Repair unreadable/malformed skins.json from a known backup; it is not silently skipped. Prefer package import/export over manual edits.

docs.title: Import validation
docs.text: Symptom Cause / action Unsupported manifest Use package schema 3, or a legacy schema-2 package without version-3 optional blocks. New packages should use 3; catalog schema 1 is not a portable package manifest. Skin appearance must contain ... Supply exactly eyes, backgrounds, eye_safe_layer, and state_effects. Disabled features still require their complete fields. Unsupported parameter Remove custom geometry, animation code, expression definitions, URLs, or unknown fields; use the reference. Unsafe archive entries Put skin.yaml at root; remove parent folders, nested assets, backslashes, traversal, symlinks, __MACOSX, .DS_Store, and ._* files. Duplicate/unreferenced entries Include each file once and only images referenced by the manifest. Omit assets/ entirely for an asset-free skin. Missing or invalid image Check exact filename/case, extension and PNG/JPEG signature; image bytes must match the extension. Import fails when states share an image The current importer writes each state's file exclusively. Give each assigned state a distinct filename, even if the bytes are identical. Size/dimension error Observe the package limits. Validate decoded dimensions on a PHOS installation with OpenCV/NumPy; this check is skipped when those modules are absent. Name imports but later metadata loading fails Use a nonempty name of at most 80 characters and description of at most 240 characters. Initial package-manifest checks are less strict than persistent custom-record checks.

docs.title: Colours, dimensions, and rendering
docs.text:
• Hex colour becomes null in YAML: quote "#RRGGBB"; unquoted # begins a comment. Iris presets are accepted and normalised; LED palettes require hex.
  • Unexpected eye-body colours: skin iris colour is separate from semantic accents and expression geometry. Test with a neutral state/expression first.
  • Background is cropped: the renderer scales proportionally to fill and centre-crops. Prepare 800×600 images for the reference display.
  • No Eye Safe halo: there must be a usable background with enough brightness or variation to need protection. A dark or absent background can produce none.
  • State Effects look static or restrained: check enablement, preset, palette, reduced motion, and actual robot state. Static SVG Preview is one frame.
  • Changed file still looks old: display background preparation is keyed by path and dimensions. Use a new asset filename or restart to invalidate an existing prepared image after replacing its bytes in place.
  • LEDs do not change: confirm the resolved skin, its enabled palette, the semantic intent, and an active LED-capable controller. Live Preview does not apply LED palettes; absent/disabled entries use runtime fallback colours.
  • Idle timing does not change: Physical Personality is skin-owned and applied during effective-skin reconciliation. Live Preview applies visual blocks only; tracking, attention, motion reactions, and system state override idle intent.

docs.title: Preview and saved-appearance differences
docs.text:
The static appearance_preview.render_preview renderer currently constructs its eye renderer without the configured shape, so non-classic shapes can look classic in SVG Preview. The preview service also constructs a repository without the optional YAML catalog; selecting a catalog-only ID in that static preview path can fail even though normal skin listing/live activation resolves it. Use the live face display for those checks.

The current appearance_snapshot helper records classic_oval rather than reading the selected shape. Internal “create from current appearance” and appearance-matching paths can therefore omit a non-classic shape. Author/export explicit skin definitions instead of relying on that capture path for shape.

Internal repository rename and update_led_palette operations currently reconstruct a custom definition without retaining physical_personality. They are not editors exposed by the current skin-card UI. Keep the authored package as the source for a skin's personality when using internal helpers.

docs.title: Activation and deletion
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / action Runtime appearance service not ready Wait until the running display/services are ready, then retry. Importing a package does not start the runtime. Saved skin differs from visible skin Check Global Appearance versus Follow Active Agent and the selected agent's current activity lease. A higher-priority eligible active agent may be visible. Preview remains after leaving the page Live Preview has no expiry timer. Apply the intended skin, reconcile normal appearance, or restart. Missing custom backgrounds Explicit Preview/Apply reports and drops missing state assignments; automatic selected-agent appearance falls back to global instead. Restore the files or export/reimport a complete package. Apply failed The application attempts to restore the previous saved configuration. Some live work may already have occurred; inspect active status and retry or use the normal restart workflow. Cannot delete skin Built-ins/catalog entries are not deletable through custom-skin deletion. Remove agent references and active owned-background references for a custom skin first. Reimport does not update an assigned skin Imports always receive a new ID. Reassign agents or select the new global skin explicitly. Warning/error LED colours ignore the theme Those semantic colours are protected and are not configurable skin keys.

These limits describe the current implementation. Skin packages do not promise compatibility with future schemas, additional image formats, custom animation engines, or arbitrary third-party renderer plugins.
